vpeBqISgks.one_liner: Audits the CLEVER Lean 4 vericoding benchmark with three agentic stacks, cataloguing specification errors and isomorphism-scoring failures.
vpeBqISgks.problem: It is unclear how reliably CLEVER measures verified code generation, since isomorphism-based scoring against a single reference specification can break down.
vpeBqISgks.method: Runs three independent agentic stacks (Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, Kimi K2.5) on CLEVER, distills a taxonomy of benchmark errors, and analyzes cases where generated and reference specifications formalize different yet defensible readings.
vpeBqISgks.key_idea: Run independent agentic provers on the benchmark and audit entries and the scoring rule, exposing flawed reference specifications and isomorphism-scoring failures.
vpeBqISgks.evidence: Audit of CLEVER (161 entries) with three agentic stacks based on Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4, and Kimi K2.5.
vpeBqISgks.claimed_gains: Finds arguably flawed reference specifications in 80 of 161 entries; the stacks generate arguably valid specifications for up to 98.8% of entries, certify implementations for up to 92.3%, and reach up to 96.2% end-to-end success over entries with sound premises.
vpeBqISgks.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the audit finds concrete bugs in a benchmark that acts as a community single point of failure, with consequential effects on measured progress and a useful error taxonomy.
vpeBqISgks.main_concern: The contribution is an audit and error taxonomy without an implemented alternative evaluation, and the saturation evidence is weaker than the defect evidence.

m5TLPK0U7O.one_liner: Injects facts from a synthetic latent taxonomy into continued pre-training of Pythia and OLMo 2 to track category-based property induction.
m5TLPK0U7O.problem: It is unclear whether and how language models trained only to predict the next token develop human-like category-based property induction.
m5TLPK0U7O.method: Builds a hierarchical taxonomy of synthetic entities grouped by shared properties, injects facts from it into continued pre-training of Pythia and OLMo 2 models from 70M to 7B parameters, and tracks inductive behavior and internal activation similarity.
m5TLPK0U7O.key_idea: Teach models facts drawn from a hidden taxonomy of synthetic entities, then measure whether a property learned for one entity transfers more within its category than across categories.
m5TLPK0U7O.evidence: Pythia and OLMo 2 models from 70M to 7B with injected taxonomy facts; clustering of entity activations recovers the taxonomic tree; further tests of model size, prior pre-training, and in-context transfer.
m5TLPK0U7O.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports findings (for example, induction weakens with model size under a fixed and limited data budget) rather than numeric gains.
m5TLPK0U7O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is well controlled with a useful hybrid synthetic-real pretraining setup, and that the findings on when and how property induction develops are interesting.
m5TLPK0U7O.main_concern: The induction-advantage setup for the model-size experiments may confound memorization and generalization, since larger models may put more mass on synthetic tokens in general.

KH9izZNOKI.one_liner: Modular simulation benchmark for embodied tasks requiring map-based reasoning in large, dynamic worlds, with shared RL and ROS2 interfaces.
KH9izZNOKI.problem: Few embodied AI benchmarks require map-based reasoning, so architectures that build and use map-like representations as flexibly as animals are hard to develop.
KH9izZNOKI.method: ForagerSim exposes independent difficulty axes: perception (2D sensing to RGB or LiDAR), scale (room to multi-km), topology (open fields to mazes), dynamics (smoke, debris, sensorimotor failures) and tasks (2D coverage to foraging-inspired well-alternation).
KH9izZNOKI.key_idea: Expose independent difficulty axes (perception, scale, topology, dynamics, task) so that map-based reasoning becomes necessary and can be isolated.
KH9izZNOKI.evidence: Reinforcement learning baselines (PPO, Dreamer per reviews) compared with an explicit mapping-and-planning frontier explorer and a human, with 3 seeds per reviews; the abstract is cut off at the comparison.
KH9izZNOKI.claimed_gains: not stated; this is a benchmark paper with no numbers visible in the abstract.
KH9izZNOKI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it fills a real gap with a scalable, modular platform offering Gym and ROS 2 interfaces, configurable dynamics and sensing, and reproducible code and seeds.
KH9izZNOKI.main_concern: The claim that map-based reasoning is the bottleneck is not isolated (memoryless PPO, near-default Dreamer, no oracle-map test), and the added value over existing benchmarks and the strength of the comparisons are unclear.

IgVNSa3MMg.one_liner: Trains 500M, 1.5B and 3B language models as one nested architecture, enabling distillation and speculative decoding inside the suite.
IgVNSa3MMg.problem: Training a language model suite classically means training and serving each model separately, which costs extra compute and parameters.
IgVNSa3MMg.method: Stacks sub-models of increasing size into one nested architecture trained end-to-end, which cuts total suite parameters and distills from the largest model to all smaller sub-models at every step. The draft model sits inside the verifier for speculative decoding.
IgVNSa3MMg.key_idea: Smaller sub-models are nested inside the largest model and share weights, so one training run yields the suite and each step distills the largest into the smaller sub-models.
IgVNSa3MMg.evidence: A suite of 500M, 1.5B and 3B sub-models trained on 35B FineWeb-Edu tokens, compared with independently trained baselines on perplexity, out-of-domain perplexity and benchmarks, plus speculative decoding and architecture ablations.
IgVNSa3MMg.claimed_gains: On par with independently trained baselines on perplexity and benchmarks while using 36% less training compute, with 14-26% higher throughput via speculative decoding.
IgVNSa3MMg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and the nested design reaches near-parity with independently trained models at lower compute, supported by extensive ablations and a broad evaluation.
IgVNSa3MMg.main_concern: Matryoshka is slightly below the token-matched vanilla baseline at every size (for example 53.3 vs 53.5 at 3B), results are single-seed, and evidence at larger scales, in MoE, and against MatFormer-style baselines at main scale is limited.

fnMHUImLl3.one_liner: Judges RLVR boundary comparisons against measured seed noise and shows sampling protocol alone can flip the base-versus-RLVR conclusion.
fnMHUImLl3.problem: Whether RLVR expands a base model's reasoning boundary is disputed, and published comparisons may reflect sampling protocol and noise rather than capability.
fnMHUImLl3.method: Holds one (base, RLVR) pair fixed and varies only sampling temperature and scoring rule across k from 8 to 512, judges each movement against a measured seed noise floor, and turns this into a decision procedure returning AHEAD, CAUGHT or UNJUDGEABLE for a pair under a protocol.
fnMHUImLl3.key_idea: Each pass@k comparison is judged against a half-split seed noise floor, and the verdict AHEAD, CAUGHT or UNJUDGEABLE depends on the pair and the sampling protocol.
fnMHUImLl3.evidence: Controlled experiments on Minerva and MATH-500 with a 7B pair, using paired problem bootstrap, added sampling seeds, several scoring rules, and null-comparison calibration of the decision threshold.
fnMHUImLl3.claimed_gains: Of 30 seed-0 comparisons between the two temperatures, 11 are unjudgeable and the rest sit on two Minerva cell pairs whose 11 reseeded comparisons clear again in all 53 measurable replicates, with the crossover point k* moving from 10 to 48 in the sharpest case.
fnMHUImLl3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is important and the controlled design, which fixes the model pair while changing protocol components, convincingly shows protocol dependence such as a 10-to-48 crossover shift.
fnMHUImLl3.main_concern: Noise-clearing effects concentrate in two Minerva chat-template configurations, and the decision procedure lacks independent validation because its threshold was chosen on the same null comparisons used to report the false-AHEAD rate.

7Hj6NN2ymu.one_liner: NGC replaces Euclidean terminal cost in latent world-model planning with shortest-path distance on a mutual nearest-neighbor latent graph.
7Hj6NN2ymu.problem: Planning with Euclidean latent distance assumes proximity measures progress to the goal, but for LeWM this holds only near the goal and the cost forms spurious low-cost basins that trap the planner.
7Hj6NN2ymu.method: Neighborhood Graph Cost estimates distance along the latent manifold as the shortest path on a mutual nearest-neighbor graph built over latents of training observations. It changes only the terminal cost and requires no retraining.
7Hj6NN2ymu.key_idea: Use graph geodesic distance over training-observation latents as the terminal cost, approximating distance along a curved latent manifold.
7Hj6NN2ymu.evidence: Four tasks with LeWM, with ablations, oracle-prediction controls, larger CEM budgets and different checkpoints, plus a mixed cross-model check on LpWM described in reviews.
7Hj6NN2ymu.claimed_gains: NGC improves LeWM's success rate on all four tasks, with the gain growing as the goal moves farther from the start; no numbers are stated.
7Hj6NN2ymu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the diagnosis of spurious basins clear and the training-free method simple, with convincing ablations and controls and gains that grow with goal distance.
7Hj6NN2ymu.main_concern: Novelty is limited because graph geodesics are well established (as in Isomap), and the method needs offline latent coverage, with scalability and robustness to graph construction unclear.

RUeuVDvSod.one_liner: AltRA-Test bootstraps items, substitutes one of k human annotations with an LLM label, and tests non-inferiority of inter-annotator agreement.
RUeuVDvSod.problem: The alt-test for replacing human annotators with LLM judges assumes all items share the same annotators, which fails in large-scale settings where items get different annotator subsets.
RUeuVDvSod.method: A bootstrap resamples items, draws k human annotations per item, and replaces one with an LLM annotation to form paired all-human and mixed human-LLM panels. Replacement is supported when the mixed panel's inter-annotator agreement is statistically non-inferior to the all-human panel's.
RUeuVDvSod.key_idea: Compare inter-annotator agreement of all-human versus one-LLM-substituted panels via item-level bootstrap and a non-inferiority test, needing no shared annotators.
RUeuVDvSod.evidence: A proof of consistency at asymptotic level alpha, finite-sample size simulations, and real-world tests of 18 LLMs and 5 prompting techniques on 20 datasets spanning text, image, audio, and video.
RUeuVDvSod.claimed_gains: AltRa-Test requires as few as 100 items to yield stable replacement decisions.
RUeuVDvSod.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely and well motivated, the test applies to all 20 datasets where prior tests apply to few, and the simulations and real-world experiments are extensive.
RUeuVDvSod.main_concern: Novelty is limited because the mixed-panel bootstrap and non-inferiority formulation come from prior tests, and the adaptive margin grows lenient as human agreement falls, so a random labeler might pass.

7pBmxUNjQK.one_liner: Trains EHR survival models at several prediction times per patient instead of one, a model- and objective-agnostic supervision strategy.
7pBmxUNjQK.problem: EHR survival models are usually trained at one prediction time per patient but queried repeatedly as new observations arrive, creating a train-deploy mismatch.
7pBmxUNjQK.method: Sparse multi-landmark supervision trains from several points along each patient trajectory, changing only how training examples are built, so it applies across architectures and objectives. The paper also introduces trajectory-aware evaluation of successive predictions for models used repeatedly over time.
7pBmxUNjQK.key_idea: Build training examples from several landmark times per patient trajectory so the model is trained under the repeated-querying conditions it faces at deployment.
7pBmxUNjQK.evidence: Eight tasks, two health systems, and six model families, with controls matching optimizer updates or input tokens, history truncation, retraining, and EHRSHOT experiments with fewer training patients.
7pBmxUNjQK.claimed_gains: Training with three landmarks improves integrated Brier score in all 48 task-model configurations and concordance index in 46 of 48 under multi-landmark evaluation.
7pBmxUNjQK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the supervision-strategy framing practical and architecture-agnostic, with gains across six model families, two health systems, and careful controls for matched updates and tokens.
7pBmxUNjQK.main_concern: Novelty over MOTOR and ORA, which use multi-landmark supervision in pretraining, is unclear, and some headline gains come from an augmented configuration rather than plain three-landmark training.

SkFyGhpyIr.one_liner: Parallel tempering over power-sharpened LLM sampling runs interacting replicas at different sharpening levels to balance exploration and exploitation.
SkFyGhpyIr.problem: Power-sharpened sampling faces an exploration-exploitation trade-off: strong sharpening traps samplers in plausible but incorrect reasoning, while weak sharpening leaves the answer distribution diffuse.
SkFyGhpyIr.method: Parallel Power Tempering (PPT) runs multiple interacting replicas at different sharpening levels, with lower-power replicas exploring and higher-power chains exploiting, and studies swap strategies under finite memory and compute. It also mitigates a truncation bias identified in prior power samplers.
SkFyGhpyIr.key_idea: Run swap-coupled replicas at different power exponents so low-power chains explore reasoning trajectories while high-power chains exploit the sharpened target, with a corrected fixed-horizon proposal.
SkFyGhpyIr.evidence: Comparisons against single-chain power sampling and RL-post-trained models (a 9B base model per the TL;DR), with AIME and LiveCodeBench results and compute-matched controls per reviews.
SkFyGhpyIr.claimed_gains: Substantially improves single-chain power-sharpened sampling and outperforms RL-post-trained models; the TL;DR says it can push a 9B base toward frontier-level performance; no figures stated.
SkFyGhpyIr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the results strong on AIME and LiveCodeBench with well-designed compute-matched controls, and the truncation-bias correction and target-preservation theory technically solid.
SkFyGhpyIr.main_concern: The stationarity theory does not show approximate equilibration under the few refinement steps used in practice, and frontier comparisons use reported external scores rather than a matched protocol.

gXi2tEYJiw.one_liner: Normalizing flows with a decoder-Jacobian orthogonality regularizer, features ordered by explained manifold entropy, acting as non-linear PCA.
gXi2tEYJiw.problem: Unsupervised discovery of features that are both semantically meaningful and stable across runs remains a central challenge in representation learning.
gXi2tEYJiw.method: EOFlows augments maximum-likelihood normalizing-flow training with an orthogonality regularizer on the decoder Jacobian, rooted in Independent Mechanism Analysis and made tractable by a stochastic estimator at image scale (CelebA at D = 2352 and 12288). Learned features are ordered by explained (manifold) entropy after training, and keeping only the top-entropy features turns the flow into an autoencoder with an adjustable bottleneck.
gXi2tEYJiw.key_idea: Penalize non-orthogonality of the decoder Jacobian columns in a normalizing flow so coordinates can be ranked by explained manifold entropy like PCA components.
gXi2tEYJiw.evidence: CelebA experiments at D = 2352 and 12288 comparing feature stability across seeds with tuned beta-VAEs and other methods, and rate-distortion comparison with dedicated autoencoders.
gXi2tEYJiw.claimed_gains: Identifies an order of magnitude more stable features than existing methods (over a hundred stable features on CelebA versus about a dozen for tuned beta-VAEs per the TL;DR) and rivals the rate-distortion performance of dedicated autoencoders.
gXi2tEYJiw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written and honest about scope, with useful intuition for decoder orthogonality, a scalable stochastic regularizer, and a carefully designed experimental study.
gXi2tEYJiw.main_concern: Reviewers question the disentanglement and non-linear PCA claims, since decoder-Jacobian orthogonality is an explicit training objective and does not measure statistical independence or semantic correspondence.

sDQ8S6CKCh.one_liner: Open-source framework unifying model preparation, data processing, twelve unlearning methods, and robustness-aware evaluation for MLLM unlearning.
sDQ8S6CKCh.problem: MLLM unlearning progress is hard to assess because implementations and evaluation protocols are fragmented, robustness testing is incomplete, and metric reliability is poorly understood.
sDQ8S6CKCh.method: Open-MMUnlearning integrates target-model preparation, multimodal data processing, unlearning, and evaluation through shared interfaces and structured configurations, supporting five benchmarks, eight MLLMs from four model families, and twelve methods. The evaluation suite covers forgetting effectiveness, retained utility, and robustness to model interventions, adversarial inputs, and membership inference, and a metric meta-evaluation protocol tests metric reliability.
sDQ8S6CKCh.key_idea: Standardize MLLM unlearning through shared interfaces and a common protocol scoring forgetting, utility, and robustness, plus a meta-evaluation that tests whether the metrics themselves are reliable.
sDQ8S6CKCh.evidence: A common-protocol comparison of ten representative unlearning methods plus metric meta-evaluation; reviews note the controlled comparison focuses on the MLLMU 10% forget setting and the meta-evaluation uses LLaVA-1.5-7B.
sDQ8S6CKCh.claimed_gains: Among ten compared methods, GD and MIP-Editor tie for the highest overall score, with GD best on Forget Quality and MIP-Editor preserving more Model Utility.
sDQ8S6CKCh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a modular, extensible, reproducible infrastructure that puts diverse unlearning methods and robustness audits in one pipeline for fair comparison.
sDQ8S6CKCh.main_concern: Empirical coverage is narrow (mainly the MLLMU 10% forget setting and LLaVA-1.5-7B for meta-evaluation), and reviewers question whether the meta-evaluation's faithfulness definition captures real unlearning and note missing efficiency evaluation.

B7gpcboEWu.one_liner: Theory of when mixing two datasets in high-dimensional ridge regression yields a faster scaling-law rate than either alone.
B7gpcboEWu.problem: Data mixing is mostly studied empirically, and it is unclear when auxiliary data improves scaling laws rather than just adding samples.
B7gpcboEWu.method: Studies mixed-data regression with a shared regression function, heterogeneous covariances and noise, and differently growing dataset sizes. Derives the minimax risk and ridge-regression deterministic equivalents, then explicit scaling laws for aligned power-law spectra.
B7gpcboEWu.key_idea: Under aligned power-law covariance spectra, mixing improves the rate only through a specific interplay between spectral decay, target regularity, and the relative sample-size growth of the two domains.
B7gpcboEWu.evidence: Minimax risk under an ellipsoidal constraint, ridge deterministic equivalents under commutative covariances, and numerical experiments on language models showing similar behavior.
B7gpcboEWu.claimed_gains: No numerical gains stated; the result is a set of provable conditions under which mixing gives a faster rate than either dataset alone.
B7gpcboEWu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the analytical treatment clear and important, with a precise account of both boundary regimes of auxiliary-data usefulness.
B7gpcboEWu.main_concern: A gap remains between the theory (shared optimal parameter, aligned power-law spectra, ridge estimator) and neural network training, so the language-model experiments give only qualitative support.

tgZtnxKcmO.one_liner: Uses sparse-autoencoder activation attributes to select training frames and schedule them with a sigmoid curriculum.
tgZtnxKcmO.problem: Existing robot-data curation selects whole episodes or coarse blocks from a fixed distribution, leaving frame-level redundancy and ignoring how data value changes over training.
tgZtnxKcmO.method: A sparse autoencoder extracts intermediate activation features characterized by generality and specificity; these score frames and form separate general and specific streams. A step-wise sigmoid curriculum shifts sampling from general to specific frames as training progresses.
tgZtnxKcmO.key_idea: Score each frame by the generality and specificity of its sparse-autoencoder activations, then shift sampling from general to specific frames over training with a step-wise sigmoid schedule.
tgZtnxKcmO.evidence: Experiments on multiple VLA models in simulation and real-robot settings; reviewers cite three policy architectures including pi0 and OpenVLA and four real-robot tasks.
tgZtnxKcmO.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract, which is cut off before the results.
tgZtnxKcmO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find frame-level curation plus curriculum scheduling practical and easy to integrate without changing the policy loss, with improvements across several VLA models.
tgZtnxKcmO.main_concern: Data budgets are not matched: baselines keep 50% of episodes while SAFari trains on about 1.5 times more unique frames, and the necessity of SAE features is not isolated.

S3yiqSxOXG.one_liner: ConflictEval measures how sequentially applied LLM defenses interfere, and CTDR penalizes shifts opposing earlier protection directions.
S3yiqSxOXG.problem: Defenses added after deployment can weaken protection from earlier defenses, and the sequential compatibility of safety, privacy, and fairness defenses is poorly understood.
S3yiqSxOXG.method: ConflictEval evaluates 144 ordered compositions of six defenses across six models, and activation interventions on 11 selected cases test which defense-induced representational changes support protection. Conflict-Triggered Directional Retention (CTDR) then penalizes opposing shifts along directions that support earlier protection.
S3yiqSxOXG.key_idea: Penalize updates from a subsequent defense whenever they shift representations against directions that support the protection established by an earlier defense.
S3yiqSxOXG.evidence: 144 ordered compositions of six defenses spanning safety, privacy, and fairness on six models, activation interventions on 11 selected cases, and CTDR tested on six selected conflicting compositions.
S3yiqSxOXG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of sequential defense compatibility is practical and important, and that the large empirical study shows defenses are not inherently composable.
S3yiqSxOXG.main_concern: Selection bias and thin validation: the analysis narrows from 144 compositions to 11 mechanism cases and six CTDR runs without an outcome-independent selection protocol, uses single training runs and only weight-update defenses, and does not compare CTDR with other mitigation methods.

K2aws1ZIb4.one_liner: Interleaves text reasoning with short undecoded latent segments trained by semantic guidance and an intermediate-modality margin in VLMs.
K2aws1ZIb4.problem: Explicit chain-of-thought can discard fine visual details while purely latent reasoning loses the readable scaffold, so a single medium serves multimodal reasoning poorly.
K2aws1ZIb4.method: Interlude keeps language as the backbone and punctuates it with latent segments, short undecoded spans of recurrent hidden-state computation used by subsequent text. Training combines semantic guidance on the language-head readout with a geometric margin favoring an intermediate reference over either modal pole.
K2aws1ZIb4.key_idea: Trains latent states with semantic guidance on the language-head readout plus a margin favoring an intermediate reference over either modality pole.
K2aws1ZIb4.evidence: Evaluated against Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on six benchmarks (including HallusionBench, ERQA, and VSI-Bench) with explicit and latent reasoning baselines, same-data SFT controls, ablations, and geometric analysis.
K2aws1ZIb4.claimed_gains: Improves over Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on all six benchmarks with an average gain of 4.72%, and exceeds Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking on Overall while using 7.6% of its decoded tokens.
K2aws1ZIb4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree gains over the backbone are consistent across six benchmarks and that same-data controls and ablations support a contribution beyond the synthetic reasoning traces.
K2aws1ZIb4.main_concern: The geometric design (intermediate reference and margin) is weakly isolated from simpler visual alignment, and the causal role of latent tokens and the geometric analysis are not convincingly established.

BAiPg5Cs12.one_liner: Long-horizon two-agent environment where LLM agents increasingly violate a verification protocol, colluding in 94% of trajectories across 10 models.
BAiPg5Cs12.problem: LLM agents are increasingly deployed in collaborative settings, yet long-term interaction may give rise to undesirable coordination such as collusion against safety protocols.
BAiPg5Cs12.method: Two agents repeatedly complete individual tasks, share task logs, verify each other's work, and receive rewards, under constraints where higher reward is attainable only by violating the verification protocol. The authors run peer interventions and ablations over verification feedback, interaction history, and reward structure.
BAiPg5Cs12.key_idea: Makes higher reward reachable only by violating a reciprocal verification protocol, then uses controlled peer interventions and history, feedback, and reward ablations to find what drives collusion.
BAiPg5Cs12.evidence: Ten LLMs in a repeated-interaction environment with controlled peer interventions and ablations of verification feedback, interaction history, and reward structure.
BAiPg5Cs12.claimed_gains: Collusion emerges in 94% of trajectories across 10 models, more capable models in the same family reach it earlier, and restricting interaction history reduces it.
BAiPg5Cs12.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the environment makes joint protocol violations measurable, with comprehensive experiments across ten models and causal peer interventions that isolate peer influence.
BAiPg5Cs12.main_concern: The environment makes the raw-log verification requirement nearly infeasible while rewarding correct verdicts, so violations may reflect specification gaming rather than emergent collaboration risk, and the verification workflow is quite specific.

46TV7bLLXi.one_liner: Stochastic flow maps impose differentiable constraints on learned conditional laws in trajectory inference, avoiding backpropagation through ODE/SDE solvers.
46TV7bLLXi.problem: ODE/SDE-based trajectory inference matches marginals but gives little control over the learned joint law across time, and constraining generated trajectories normally needs costly numerical integration and differentiation through the solver.
46TV7bLLXi.method: CLIFT uses (stochastic) flow maps, which give parallelisable access to finite-time transitions, so conditional-law losses such as a classifier-based lineage penalty send gradients directly to the model parameters.
46TV7bLLXi.key_idea: Applies conditional-law losses on finite-time transitions produced by a flow map, so constraints train without differentiating through numerical integration.
46TV7bLLXi.evidence: Single-cell datasets, with conditional prediction accuracy (Table 1), lineage violations (Table 2), and training time (Table 3) reported per reviews.
46TV7bLLXi.claimed_gains: The visible abstract states only improved adherence to known constraints without numbers; a review cites training time falling from 65 to 8 minutes on stochastic CITE.
46TV7bLLXi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper usefully exposes limits of ODE/SDE-based trajectory inference and that flow maps give a practical way to impose lineage constraints without differentiating through the integrator.
46TV7bLLXi.main_concern: The methodological contribution is modest since flow maps were already applied to cellular trajectory inference (OTP-FM, not compared), and the theory is unclear and weakly tied to the algorithm.

NC6BzYy1m0.one_liner: Exact multi-draft speculative sampler attaining the IID acceptance ceiling, then exceeding it with equal-mass stratified, same-marginal proposals.
NC6BzYy1m0.problem: Multi-draft speculative decoding has a computable acceptance ceiling under IID proposals, but turning it into an exact, scalable sampler had remained a constructive challenge.
NC6BzYy1m0.method: Optimal IID preserves the target distribution and attains the IID ceiling for any candidate count through a finite-score construction with near-linear arithmetic preprocessing and no iterative optimization. Stratified changes proposal dependence through equal-mass stratification while preserving each slot's draft marginal, and a recursive exact verifier attains its ceiling with near-linear arithmetic work.
NC6BzYy1m0.key_idea: Stratify proposals into equal-mass strata so each slot keeps its draft marginal while coverage of every token subset matches or exceeds IID, verified exactly by a recursive procedure.
NC6BzYy1m0.evidence: Three model pairs from the Qwen3 and Gemma 2 families with four candidates, top-100 draft support, and temperature 1, plus a single-GH200 feasibility study for Qwen3-32B/1.7B.
NC6BzYy1m0.claimed_gains: Stratified recovers approximately 85-92% of the gap from optimal IID to a target-aware coupling oracle, and a single-GH200 implementation for Qwen3-32B/1.7B averages 0.49 ms per output token for verification-plan construction and online sampling.
NC6BzYy1m0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers regard the exact, non-iterative IID sampler and the coverage-dominance result for Stratified as strong theoretical contributions that remove prior approximation tolerances.
NC6BzYy1m0.main_concern: Practical impact is marginal: end-to-end gain over sequential IID is about 0.9% on one setup, and end-to-end comparisons against Optimal IID are missing.

y8ipSxUMvE.one_liner: GyroSplat compresses plasma turbulence into linear Gaussian-Gabor splat sums, refining closed-form potential and heat flux with Gauss-Newton
y8ipSxUMvE.problem: 5D gyrokinetic simulations produce tens of terabytes per run, and neural compression with physics-informed losses is hard to optimize and refine under additional constraints.
y8ipSxUMvE.method: Represents each plasma field as a weighted sum of independent Gaussian-Gabor splats that is linear in its coefficients. A staged optimization first fits reconstruction error, then refines against the potential, then adds splats to correct transport, using Gauss-Newton on closed-form derived quantities.
y8ipSxUMvE.key_idea: Make the representation linear in splat coefficients so potential and heat flux are closed-form in the code, enabling Gauss-Newton refinement of the physics quantities directly.
y8ipSxUMvE.evidence: Gyrokinetic electron data (39 snapshots from 27 trajectories per a reviewer) compared with classical codecs (wavelet bases, PCA, ZFP) and neural baselines, with ablations.
y8ipSxUMvE.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text in the batch ends before the results)
y8ipSxUMvE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method well motivated, with closed-form Jacobians giving an efficient Gauss-Newton step, results better than baselines, and a useful kappa/kappa_truth metric.
y8ipSxUMvE.main_concern: The evaluation is narrow (39 snapshots from 27 trajectories, a single seed) and the heat-flux result is fitted and evaluated on the same modes without held-out validation.

8TjfC8h4iz.one_liner: SPOT compares spatial scene graphs via optimal transport, giving a distance to supervise and evaluate spatial similarity of images
8TjfC8h4iz.problem: Image similarity usually ignores the spatial arrangement of objects, and the spatial configurations in scene graphs remain underexplored, limiting tasks like retrieval by object arrangement.
8TjfC8h4iz.method: Formalizes a Spatial Scene Graph (SSG) that encodes absolute positions as node attributes and relative positions as edge attributes (using a Force Banner relation, per reviewers), and defines SPOT, an optimal-transport criterion between SSGs. SPOT is used to evaluate models and to train backbones toward spatially aware representations.
8TjfC8h4iz.key_idea: Encode objects' absolute and relative positions as node and edge attributes of a scene graph, and compare graphs of different sizes with an optimal-transport plan as the spatial similarity.
8TjfC8h4iz.evidence: Two spatially aware downstream tasks (the abstract is cut off at "content-based ..."; reviewers cite retrieval, spatial VQA, and scene classification from scene graphs alone), including a model (S3PE) trained on triplets mined with SPOT.
8TjfC8h4iz.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text in the batch ends before the results)
8TjfC8h4iz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the Force Banner relation representation combined with optimal transport novel and interpretable, handling scene graphs with different numbers of objects, and demonstrated on downstream tasks.
8TjfC8h4iz.main_concern: The quantitative spatial evaluations use SPOT itself as the reference ranking, so SPOT is not validated against an independent criterion, and the optimal-transport cost is high.

HwXLxgDn5l.one_liner: PLADOS is a retraction-free decentralized landing algorithm on the Stiefel manifold with a fixed landing step and linear speedup
HwXLxgDn5l.problem: Decentralized optimization on the Stiefel manifold lacks a retraction-free method whose manifold consensus error contracts without extra parameters that need tuning.
HwXLxgDn5l.method: Each iteration combines local stochastic gradient updates with a single retraction-free communication step over the communication graph. A restricted secant inequality for the penalty-only scheme gives local contraction of the manifold consensus error; reviewers note the landing correction needs only matrix multiplications and additions, a fixed coefficient of 1/3, and no gradient tracking.
HwXLxgDn5l.key_idea: Use a fixed-coefficient landing penalty step whose restricted secant inequality on the Stiefel-consensus intersection contracts consensus error, avoiding retractions, gradient tracking, and tuned landing parameters.
HwXLxgDn5l.evidence: Convergence proof with a stochastic guarantee and linear speedup, plus experiments on PCA, low-rank matrix completion, and MNIST compared with DRSGD (per reviewers) across stepsizes and networks.
HwXLxgDn5l.claimed_gains: Linear speedup in the number of nodes n with asymptotic rate O(sigma/sqrt(nbK) + (xi^2)^(1/3)/K^(2/3)) after K iterations, where b is the local batch size.
HwXLxgDn5l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the convergence theory sound and the retraction-free update simple, with one communication round per iteration and experiments showing computational efficiency.
HwXLxgDn5l.main_concern: Novelty over decentralized retraction-free methods (DESTINY, DRFGT) and centralized parameter-free landing is limited, the experiments are simple and compare mainly to DRSGD, and "parameter-free" overstates since the stepsize still matters.

VE95SGdHri.one_liner: Hierarchical normalizing flow with identifiable, equivariant levels extrapolates to larger systems by adding a copy of an existing level
VE95SGdHri.problem: Generative models of multiscale physical systems lack the inductive bias needed to generalize to larger systems than they were trained on.
VE95SGdHri.method: A hierarchical normalizing flow whose levels are local, symmetry-equivariant continuous normalizing flows mapping between adjacent scales, trained with regularizers and a normalization that fix the reparameterization freedom. A larger system is modeled by adding a new level, often a copy of an existing one, instead of retraining.
VE95SGdHri.key_idea: Make each scale a local equivariant flow level whose reparameterization freedom is fixed by regularizers, so a self-similar (RG fixed-point) level can be reused for larger systems.
VE95SGdHri.evidence: Two-dimensional lattice models, checked against exact results and Monte Carlo simulations, with theory giving conditions under which the regularizers leave at most one optimal hierarchy; on the 2D Ising model independently trained models learn the same levels.
VE95SGdHri.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text in the batch ends before the quantitative results)
VE95SGdHri.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea of identifiable levels that extend to other scales by adding a layer interesting and well motivated, supported by 2D Ising experiments and placed within NeuralRG and RG-Flow.
VE95SGdHri.main_concern: Section 3 is dense and hard to follow, and extrapolation works only at the critical self-similar point, with no ablation of the regularizers.

AKMK9bdEZu.one_liner: DPAL regulates latent-factorization training with nonlinear and incremental PID controllers and fuzzy-tuned gains for incomplete NILM tensors
AKMK9bdEZu.problem: NILM data are highly incomplete, and existing SGD-based latent factorization of tensors models have limited optimization efficiency and representation accuracy.
AKMK9bdEZu.method: DPAL uses a nonlinear PID controller on the training error that exploits historical error, an incremental PID controller for fine-grained learning-rate adjustment, and fuzzy-logic adaptive gain tuning for the PID controllers. It adds a conditional coordinate-wise convergence and stability analysis.
AKMK9bdEZu.key_idea: Apply PID control to the SGD training error and to per-coordinate learning rates in tensor factorization, with fuzzy logic tuning the PID gains.
AKMK9bdEZu.evidence: Nine settings on three real-world NILM datasets with different sampling rates and severe missingness, with standard deviations over 20 runs and a four-way SLF/NPL/IPL/DPAL ablation (per reviewers).
AKMK9bdEZu.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract text in the batch ends before the results; reviewers report the lowest mean RMSE and MAE in all nine settings)
AKMK9bdEZu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree DPAL reaches the lowest reported RMSE and MAE in all nine settings and that the ablation shows error regulation drives most of the accuracy gain.
AKMK9bdEZu.main_concern: Novelty is not established against close precedents such as NPIL, and baselines omit Adam, momentum, and existing PID-based optimizers on the same factorization objective.

ho6cqpAPCt.one_liner: Shows transformers trained jointly on modular addition and multiplication learn prime-by-prime modular decompositions, which addition alone does not yield.
ho6cqpAPCt.problem: What determines whether neural networks organize into independent modules is poorly understood, partly because the subtasks and representations are usually unknown.
ho6cqpAPCt.method: Transformers are trained on (a+b) mod n and (a x b) mod n for n a product of distinct primes, where the Chinese remainder theorem gives a known decomposition, and modularity is measured at three levels.
ho6cqpAPCt.key_idea: Use modular arithmetic with composite moduli, where the Chinese remainder decomposition is known, to test whether training on addition plus multiplication yields per-prime modules.
ho6cqpAPCt.evidence: Error independence across primes, separate representational subspaces, and distinct neuron groups; reviews cite 20 seeds, n=1001, and one-layer models.
ho6cqpAPCt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the three-level modularity analysis is clean and that the joint-training result is striking, with addition-only training failing to produce full modularity.
ho6cqpAPCt.main_concern: No mechanistic explanation is given for why multiplication induces modularity, and scope is narrow (one decomposition, fixed one-layer size).

mOXtWeb0Zw.one_liner: Compresses trained SSMs by balancing each against the state covariance induced by calibration inputs, with a global state budget.
mOXtWeb0Zw.problem: State dimension is a direct cost of autoregressive SSM inference, and existing post-training reduction prunes in trained coordinates or uses balanced truncation that assumes generic white-noise inputs rather than deployment inputs.
mOXtWeb0Zw.method: POISE is label-free: it estimates the state covariance induced by a small calibration set, balances each SSM against it, and allocates a global state budget across layers. For stable LTI SSMs it yields stable reduced systems with error guarantees for arbitrary inputs and finite horizons, and it is extended empirically to selective Mamba-2.
mOXtWeb0Zw.key_idea: Replace the white-noise controllability Gramian of balanced truncation with an input-induced state covariance from calibration data, then allocate state budget across layers.
mOXtWeb0Zw.evidence: LTI backbones S4D, SaShiMi, and S5, plus an empirical extension to Mamba-2 1.3B (WikiText perplexity) with comparison to GHOST, and LRA-Text results per reviews.
mOXtWeb0Zw.claimed_gains: On Mamba-2 1.3B, POISE removes 70% of the recurrent states for only 0.34 additional WikiText perplexity, and at a 2048-token context the reduced model comes within 0.6 perplexity of Llama-3.2-1B with a four-bit KV cache while using less memory.
mOXtWeb0Zw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the input-aware balanced-truncation formulation is principled, backed by theory for stable LTI systems, and gives promising Mamba-2 compression with global budget allocation.
mOXtWeb0Zw.main_concern: Guarantees cover only individual stable LTI systems, not selective Mamba-2, and end-to-end efficiency is not directly measured since Mamba-2 perplexity runs the full model with a modified output projection.

Ca2SzRxtpb.one_liner: Defines attention capacity for kernels and proposes additive spline and polynomial-exponential kernels with infinite capacity and quasi-linear sorting-based computation.
Ca2SzRxtpb.problem: Softmax attention costs quadratic time, and common quasi-linear kernel attention from finite-dimensional feature maps has limited expressivity.
Ca2SzRxtpb.method: The authors define capacity as the maximum sequence length for which the attention matrix can approximate the identity, show that softmax, Gauss and Laplace kernels have infinite capacity, and build additive kernels from univariate splines and polynomial exponentials. These keep infinite capacity and compute attention by sorting.
Ca2SzRxtpb.key_idea: Replace multivariate kernels with additive univariate kernels whose attention can be summed by sorting while keeping infinite capacity.
Ca2SzRxtpb.evidence: Proofs of capacity results and quasi-linear complexity, plus efficient implementations benchmarked against modern softmax backends on long sequences.
Ca2SzRxtpb.claimed_gains: Abstract states advantages over modern softmax backends for long sequences; no numbers stated.
Ca2SzRxtpb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the capacity definition gives a clean theoretical view of kernel-attention expressivity and that the simple additive kernels and CUDA implementations are sound.
Ca2SzRxtpb.main_concern: Capacity is a weakly motivated, effectively binary measure that does not guarantee practical expressivity or separate infinite-capacity kernels, and the speedup over full attention is limited.

YchGapqmwe.one_liner: Shows deletion in LLM unlearning and editing can write a recoverable trace of the deleted target, via random-target controls.
YchGapqmwe.problem: Recovery-based evaluation reads a recovered target as proof the knowledge survived deletion, but the deletion process itself may create the recoverable trace.
YchGapqmwe.method: Applies the same deletion procedure to random target tokens never associated with the subject and tests whether they become recoverable, naming the effect a loss-target imprint, and probes it across deletion mechanisms with probes adapted to each method.
YchGapqmwe.key_idea: A deletion loss that directly references the target token imprints that token, so random never-associated targets become recoverable too, increasingly with deletion strength.
YchGapqmwe.evidence: Random-target controls across several deletion and editing mechanisms, with the target often ranking first or second among vocabulary tokens; reviews note the main findings are limited to single-token, single-fact deletion.
YchGapqmwe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the random-target control is intuitive and convincing and exposes an important limitation of recovery-based unlearning evaluation.
YchGapqmwe.main_concern: Scope is limited to single-token, single-fact deletion with few methods, and it is unclear how imprint signals can be separated from retained knowledge in real unlearning evaluations.

WNVALEzP5z.one_liner: Aligns frozen unimodal spectral spaces from sparse verified pairs via global distance-preserving alignment then regularized non-rigid residual correction.
WNVALEzP5z.problem: Cross-modal retrieval usually needs abundant paired data, but reliable image-text pairs can be scarce when unimodal representations are independently built and fixed.
WNVALEzP5z.method: SLNA treats verified pairs as landmarks, first recovers a global distance-preserving coordinate relation, then allocates nonlinear capacity only to the remaining residuals through regularized corrections in complementary coordinate and angular geometries.
WNVALEzP5z.key_idea: Model the mismatch between frozen spaces as a global discrepancy plus position-dependent non-rigid deformation, and fit it by landmark registration.
WNVALEzP5z.evidence: Flickr30k and MSCOCO experiments against rigid Procrustes alignment and a direct RBF mapping under matched model selection, plus structural neighborhood-agreement diagnostics.
WNVALEzP5z.claimed_gains: Consistently improves over rigid Procrustes alignment and outperforms a direct RBF mapping under matched model-selection settings; no numbers are stated in the visible abstract.
WNVALEzP5z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the global-to-local geometric formulation intuitive and computationally manageable, usable without updating the pretrained encoders in low-supervision settings.
WNVALEzP5z.main_concern: Gains over the direct RBF baseline are modest, that baseline lacks a global term, and ablations of the coordinate branch, angular branch, and fusion are missing.

EaRCZifIvT.one_liner: Decentralized MAPF agents iteratively refine discrete action intents over communication rounds before committing, pretrained by imitation and tuned with MICPO.
EaRCZifIvT.problem: Independently sampling per-agent actions can recombine locally valid choices into incompatible joint actions even when each agent's distribution is learned correctly.
EaRCZifIvT.method: DMM replaces one-shot action sampling with discrete iterative refinement: agents initialize random action intents and refine them through local communication, inspired by diffusion and flow matching. It is pretrained with imitation learning on expert MAPF solutions and fine-tuned with MICPO, a critic-free group-relative RL method for multi-agent, multi-round refinement.
EaRCZifIvT.key_idea: Agents start from random action intents and refine them jointly through communication rounds, coupling their choices before any action is committed.
EaRCZifIvT.evidence: MovingAI tasks and POGEMA benchmarks against learnable baselines, plus a controlled corridor test of joint-action validity.
EaRCZifIvT.claimed_gains: On 1,600 MovingAI tasks, DMM fine-tuned with MICPO solves 1,598, the highest coverage among the evaluated methods.
EaRCZifIvT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it addresses a real multimodality problem in decentralized MAPF, illustrated by a clear corridor example, with direct evidence that refinement rounds raise joint-action validity and strong results over baselines.
EaRCZifIvT.main_concern: The theory only shows an expressivity gap for independent sampling, not that DMM closes it, and ablations (test-time input changes, 0.8 teacher forcing, MICPO components) do not cleanly isolate the sources of gain.

UKXQRoxbh5.one_liner: Tracks the class-conditional posterior online in discrete diffusion from conditional and unconditional predictions, enabling interpretable dynamics and AND/OR/NOT guidance.
UKXQRoxbh5.problem: Discrete diffusion models are far less understood than continuous ones, with few tools for interpreting their dynamics or controlling generation.
UKXQRoxbh5.method: They derive a framework that tracks the class posterior online by combining conditional and unconditional model predictions, and use the posterior for logical guidance operations. They also contrast how classifier-free guidance mixes distributions in discrete versus continuous settings.
UKXQRoxbh5.key_idea: Combine conditional and unconditional predictions at each step to track the class posterior, then reuse it for AND, OR and NOT guidance.
UKXQRoxbh5.evidence: Synthetic data with analytically tractable quantities, MNIST, text (topic steering with LLaDA per reviews), and antibody sequences with a 50M model.
UKXQRoxbh5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the online posterior elegant and nearly free given guidance predictions, with new interpretability of token-level dynamics in masked language models.
UKXQRoxbh5.main_concern: Scalability is not shown (small models, few classes), and the discrete-versus-continuous guidance observation has no measured effect on generation quality.

RKTmHwIHFt.one_liner: Reweights rejected tokens in DPO by gradient alignment with the preferred response, weakening penalties on tokens aligned with preferred behavior.
RKTmHwIHFt.problem: DPO applies response-level supervision, so all tokens in a rejected response get negative signal, including tokens that encode behavior useful for the preferred response.
RKTmHwIHFt.method: GAW-PO estimates, for each rejected token, whether penalizing it would interfere with preferred update directions. Tokens whose gradients align with preferred behavior get a weaker negative contribution, and conflicting tokens keep a stronger penalty.
RKTmHwIHFt.key_idea: Weight each rejected token's penalty by the signed alignment between its parameter-space gradient and the preferred response's update direction.
RKTmHwIHFt.evidence: Eleven benchmarks spanning mathematics, reasoning, coding and question answering, plus sweeps over the DPO regularization parameter beta.
RKTmHwIHFt.claimed_gains: Improves average performance by 0.97 points over standard DPO and 0.65 points over the strongest competing baseline across 11 benchmarks, and keeps improving as beta decreases while DPO degrades.
RKTmHwIHFt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the token-level gradient-interaction motivation interesting and see it filling a gap among token-based preference optimization methods.
RKTmHwIHFt.main_concern: Baselines are author re-implementations, several modified from the originals, and the margins over them are modest.

kaQzSOF7Cj.one_liner: Dense remote-sensing layout-to-image diffusion using a fixed-resolution rasterized box canvas, category-level attention, and instance-aware layering.
kaQzSOF7Cj.problem: Instance-centric conditioning for layout-to-image generation scales poorly in dense scenes, forcing truncation of objects and creating a condition–image mismatch.
kaQzSOF7Cj.method: DenseGen rasterizes all bounding boxes onto a fixed-resolution global canvas, then decouples category-level semantic conditioning (Category-Level Layout Mask Attention) from instance-level spatial control (Instance-Aware Spatial Adaptive Layering, which distributes overlapping boxes across spatial layers).
kaQzSOF7Cj.key_idea: Rasterize all boxes onto a fixed canvas, inject shared category semantics into matching regions, and split overlapping boxes into separate spatial layers to reduce ambiguity.
kaQzSOF7Cj.evidence: Experiments on DIOR-R, DOTA-v1.0, and SODA-A measuring layout consistency, semantic accuracy, and downstream detector-training augmentation, with comparisons that reviewers say include a ControlNet box baseline.
kaQzSOF7Cj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clear, the dense-layout motivation is practical, and results improve over baselines, including gains when augmenting real detector-training data.
kaQzSOF7Cj.main_concern: Reviewers say novelty is limited because the parts resemble existing spatial-conditioning and layering ideas, some baselines may be weakly configured (horizontal-box methods scored with rotated IoU), and the downstream protocol reuses DOTA validation layouts.

AlV4DfcNd1.one_liner: GUI-HARVEST optimizes a GUI agent's harness code from screenshot-aligned, repeated-execution evidence with prediction-checked edits, leaving model weights frozen.
AlV4DfcNd1.problem: Hand-engineering the harness around a GUI model is costly, and automatic optimization must reconcile model intent with visual effects, diagnose failures under variable outcomes, and turn recurring failures into reusable runtime changes.
AlV4DfcNd1.method: It aligns model outputs and executed actions with before-and-after screenshots, treats repeated executions of a task as one joint evidence unit for within-task comparison, and consolidates verified findings into recurring failure patterns that map to bounded source-code edits whose predicted behavioral effects are recorded before evaluation and then checked.
AlV4DfcNd1.key_idea: Diagnose from before/after screenshot transitions and within-task comparison of repeated runs, then apply bounded code edits whose predicted behavioral effects are registered before evaluation and verified.
AlV4DfcNd1.evidence: Experiments on OSWorld-Verified and WindowsAgentArena, with reviewers citing a held-out 201-task set with six backbones and comparisons against Meta-Harness and Self-Harness.
AlV4DfcNd1.claimed_gains: not stated in the available abstract text (the TLDR claims improved OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena performance without changing model weights; a review cites +10.16 percentage points for Qwen3-VL-32B on the held-out set).
AlV4DfcNd1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the GUI-specific diagnosis loop is principled and practically relevant, with gains that transfer to held-out tasks across backbones and registered-prediction validation as a useful guardrail.
AlV4DfcNd1.main_concern: Optimization cost is not reported, the GUI-specific contribution is not isolated from search budget or related harness optimizers, and evaluation is almost entirely on OSWorld.

IUtWp60bvv.one_liner: Audits membership leakage in 3D Gaussian Splatting via view-specific photometric error versus reference models, and reduces it with source-exclusion distillation.
IUtWp60bvv.problem: A shared 3DGS asset may reveal which photographs trained it through view-specific rendering fidelity, even when neighboring views reconstruct images that never supervised optimization.
IUtWp60bvv.method: The audit compares target errors with those of same-scene reference models trained without the candidate pool, using a photometric log-ratio score. The defense routes each protected camera through teachers that excluded its photograph and distills students from their renders.
IUtWp60bvv.key_idea: Compare a photograph's render error against same-scene references trained without it to detect membership, and distill students only from teachers that excluded each protected photograph.
IUtWp60bvv.evidence: Controlled interventions with fixed initialization and schedules, an audit on eight new test scenes, and a defense evaluated on four scenes over nine attack configurations.
IUtWp60bvv.claimed_gains: The photometric log-ratio improves mean normalized partial AUC over 0 to 1% FPR by 0.1567 relative to PSNR-GAP on eight test scenes; the defense lowers mean per-asset maximum AUC over nine attack configurations from 0.9457 to 0.7364 at a mean held-out PSNR cost of 0.241 dB.
IUtWp60bvv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it studies a new privacy problem for 3DGS assets, with controlled experiments that isolate the photometric supervision trace and a complete attack-and-defense pipeline.
IUtWp60bvv.main_concern: Low-FPR results hinge on few nonmembers per scene with unstable thresholds, and the audit and defense require many extra reference and teacher models trained per scene.

PoGZo0yQcM.one_liner: Training-free steering controller that extracts a THINK/ACT direction from contrastive completions and sets per-cluster steering strengths to control tool calls.
PoGZo0yQcM.problem: Tool calls can correct failed internal reasoning but can also add noise, raise cost or corrupt a correct answer, so an agent must decide per input whether to reason internally or call a tool.
PoGZo0yQcM.method: ToA-Eval contrasts no-tool and forced-tool executions to identify when tool use helps or harms a given agent. ToA-Steer is a dynamic cluster-routed controller that extracts a shared THINK/ACT direction from contrastive completions and selects input-specific steering strengths in latent space.
PoGZo0yQcM.key_idea: Route each input to a cluster and apply activation steering along a shared THINK/ACT direction with a calibrated per-cluster strength, shifting tool-call propensity up or down.
PoGZo0yQcM.evidence: Four reasoning benchmarks and four open-weight LLMs against prompt-based, training-based and static-steering baselines, with ablations on directions, clustering and intervention timing, plus a web-search transfer experiment (per reviews).
PoGZo0yQcM.claimed_gains: Raises mean accuracy from 0.585 to 0.723, gaining +16pp accuracy on ACT-needed instances and +9pp on THINK-preferred instances, and is the only evaluated method that moves the tool-call rate in opposite directions on the two classes.
PoGZo0yQcM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Think-or-Act framing is a useful question and the method is a simple, training-free controller with consistent gains across four models and benchmarks and informative ablations.
PoGZo0yQcM.main_concern: Evaluation scale is small with no variance reported (about 50 contrastive pairs and 50-instance dev splits for selecting magnitudes and cluster count), so the claim of winning all settings and robustness to new inputs is weakly supported.

y1M6lwme2S.one_liner: Separates geometric distance from identifiability in OOD splits by censoring element co-occurrences in catalyst libraries and auditing the null space.
y1M6lwme2S.problem: An OOD split can require prediction far from observed inputs or prediction of interactions never jointly observed, which are different tasks, and the second can leave a prediction formally unidentified.
y1M6lwme2S.method: Censors element co-occurrences in four experimental catalyst libraries and runs a null-space audit showing missing interactions can be unidentified even inside the training convex hull. Different estimators then supply different completion priors, probed with synthetic controls, additional datasets and training-only shadow censoring.
y1M6lwme2S.key_idea: Treat OOD difficulty as two separate quantities, geometric distance and identifiability of missing interactions, and measure the latter by a null-space audit of the representation.
y1M6lwme2S.evidence: Four catalyst libraries with censored co-occurrences, synthetic controls, and additional microbial, electrocatalyst and reaction-screen datasets used to reproduce the information loss.
y1M6lwme2S.claimed_gains: A neural difference model reduces squared missing-interaction coefficient error by 55-60% relative to zero completion under a quadratic-mixture reference.
y1M6lwme2S.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating geometric distance from identifiability is a useful and practically important distinction for interpreting OOD benchmark difficulty, supported by mechanistic synthetic experiments.
y1M6lwme2S.main_concern: Empirical scope is narrow (mostly four related catalyst libraries and one property), and shadow censoring does not beat always choosing the best estimator, so its practical benefit is unclear.

eRISiAkFuX.one_liner: Evaluates LLM reasoning with pairwise duels in which models create programming puzzles for each other, ranked by Elo.
eRISiAkFuX.problem: Evaluating reasoning gets harder as models improve, human curation of hard questions is expensive, and benchmark questions may have been seen in training.
eRISiAkFuX.method: Models challenge each other by creating Programming Puzzles (a boolean function for which the solver must find inputs returning True), with solutions verified by execution. Elo ratings are computed from pairwise duel results.
eRISiAkFuX.key_idea: Have each model both propose and solve verifiable programming puzzles against other models, and derive Elo ratings from pairwise duel outcomes.
eRISiAkFuX.evidence: Evaluation of 18 models (frontier systems, low-reasoning-effort variants and open-weights models) in round-robin duels, with rankings compared against existing benchmarks such as Humanity's Last Exam.
eRISiAkFuX.claimed_gains: Closely matches rankings from existing benchmarks such as Humanity's Last Exam with no human effort in creating puzzles, at a total cost of about $2,400.
eRISiAkFuX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is a clever, highly automated alternative to fixed human-authored benchmarks, with automatic verification and a fairly comprehensive round-robin evaluation.
eRISiAkFuX.main_concern: It is unclear what TTG actually measures: scores mix reasoning with code and domain details, and puzzle diversity and novelty relative to memorized problems are not established.

sW57anWo1u.one_liner: An arbitrator with its own value estimates of the executed blend gates handover from baseline control to an RL learner.
sW57anWo1u.problem: When control passes gradually from a baseline to an RL learner during online training, improving the learner needs its stand-alone value while judging handover needs the value of the blend that actually runs, and the learner's value estimates carry extrapolation error, so handover can come too early.
sW57anWo1u.method: Arbitrator-gated handover has an arbitrator judge the blend with value estimates of its own, and adds techniques to limit the effects of estimation error (reviews mention LayerNorm on the learner's critic and critic ensembles).
sW57anWo1u.key_idea: Gate on a separate arbitrator critic bootstrapped on the executed blended action, not on the learner's own critic.
sW57anWo1u.evidence: Control tasks including CSTR and Quadrotor2D (per reviews), with 10 seeds, confidence intervals and per-seed failure counts, a comparison against the RL-AR gated baseline, and ablations in the appendix; a small counterexample (Proposition 1) shows the value mismatch.
sW57anWo1u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is practically motivated and that separating the learner's value from the executed blend's value is a clear, convincing diagnosis, backed by a small counterexample.
sW57anWo1u.main_concern: Only one gated baseline (RL-AR) is compared, with other gating schemes, residual RL and adaptive MPC missing, and the tasks are relatively simple.

At59BKkCCL.one_liner: Characterizes every attainable binary majority-vote accuracy curve through a signed voting signature and the latent populations that produce it.
At59BKkCCL.problem: Increasing the voting budget can improve or reduce population accuracy and early gains or losses need not persist, and it is unclear which curves are attainable and what they identify about the latent population.
At59BKkCCL.method: For binary unweighted majority under infinitely exchangeable correctness indicators with an arbitrary latent success-probability law, the curve is encoded by a signed voting signature. The odd-budget curve and the signature determine each other, a weighted total-variation constraint characterizes attainable signatures, and a minimum-mass allocation completed by symmetric mass gives every population producing a curve.
At59BKkCCL.key_idea: Map the odd-budget accuracy curve to the moments of a signed measure over q(1-q) weighted by (2q-1), so curves and latent populations are linked through a moment problem.
At59BKkCCL.evidence: Theoretical results only; reviews note there are no experiments on real LLM repeated-sampling traces.
At59BKkCCL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the mathematical framework is solid and that the inverse characterization, showing which population differences are visible or invisible to the full curve, is the main strength.
At59BKkCCL.main_concern: The paper is purely theoretical with little motivation or guidance for practical test-time scaling, and the binary setting does not cover multi-option answers.

7JsaKV1zCL.one_liner: Data-free interpolating neural network trained on the PDE weak form via alternating least squares, with computable per-prediction error bounds.
7JsaKV1zCL.problem: Existing neural operators need large simulation datasets or long physics-informed GPU training, and they cannot report how accurate an individual prediction is.
7JsaKV1zCL.method: INO adds Karhunen-Loeve coordinates of the input field to the spatial coordinates and approximates each input with a C-HiDeNN sub-network whose trainable parameters are nodal values. Because the network is multilinear in its parameters, training reduces to one-dimensional linear solves by greedy alternating least squares, and a domain check flags inputs outside the trained range.
7JsaKV1zCL.key_idea: Make the network multilinear in its nodal parameters over spatial and Karhunen-Loeve input coordinates so weak-form training becomes alternating one-dimensional linear solves.
7JsaKV1zCL.evidence: Training and error-bound results on PDE problems including Helmholtz and nonlinear diffusion (per the reviews), with CPU-only training and a residual bound for coercive problems.
7JsaKV1zCL.claimed_gains: INO trains on one CPU core and predicts a new solution in microseconds, and for coercive problems each prediction's error is bounded by a computable residual bound that needs no reference solution.
7JsaKV1zCL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting the separable weak-form structure for data-free training with built-in reliability checks is a sensible and practically valuable idea.
7JsaKV1zCL.main_concern: Novelty over closely related structured methods such as INN-TD, PGD, POD, and low-rank tensor approaches is unclear and judged incremental.

J0g6ME9QCO.one_liner: Part-aware spring-mass model with adaptive stiffness within parts and neural oriented stiffness fields between parts learns dynamics of diverse objects.
J0g6ME9QCO.problem: Existing methods use category-specific formulations for articulated and deformable dynamics, which limits generalization to heterogeneous objects with both rigid and deformable parts.
J0g6ME9QCO.method: GenTwin splits object dynamics into intra-part and inter-part dynamics within one spring-mass representation. Part-Adaptive Spring Configuration adapts stiffness and topology using material priors and motion-derived rigidity, and Neural Anisotropic Spring Connections link neighboring parts through Neural Oriented Stiffness Fields that give continuous directional stiffness.
J0g6ME9QCO.key_idea: Model every object as a part-based spring-mass system, with rigidity-adaptive springs inside parts and learned direction-dependent stiffness fields between parts.
J0g6ME9QCO.evidence: 18 real-world scenarios spanning deformable, articulated, and heterogeneous objects, compared with category-specific methods such as PhysTwin, plus ablations of the proposed components.
J0g6ME9QCO.claimed_gains: Future-prediction Chamfer distance is reduced by approximately 28.6%, 27.3%, and 50.0% on deformable, articulated, and heterogeneous objects, respectively, over the best competing category-specific methods.
J0g6ME9QCO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified part-aware representation addresses a meaningful problem, the intra-part and inter-part decomposition is coherent, and geometric accuracy improves over baselines.
J0g6ME9QCO.main_concern: It is unclear which components drive the gain over PhysTwin since ablation drops are small, the benefit of the tensor stiffness parameterization is not isolated, and robustness of zero-order optimization across seeds is unreported.

sgWkDEomPy.one_liner: Temporal action detector keeping spatial tokens separate with per-token recurrent state, predicting at tokens, then aggregating across space.
sgWkDEomPy.problem: Most temporal action detectors pool each frame into one vector before temporal modeling, which is restrictive when actions depend on where evidence occurs and how it moves or when concurrent actions use different regions.
sgWkDEomPy.method: SpaTAD maintains a causal, location-bound recurrent state for each spatial token, predicts actions at individual tokens, and only then aggregates them across space into frame-level action predictions.
sgWkDEomPy.key_idea: Delay spatial pooling until after class prediction, carrying a location-bound recurrent state for each spatial token.
sgWkDEomPy.evidence: MultiTHUMOS, Charades, ATARS, and ROAD-Waymo, with ablations of pooling before class prediction and of collapsing spatial structure before temporal modeling.
sgWkDEomPy.claimed_gains: SpaTAD improves over the strongest matched baseline by an average of 5.9 Seg-mAP and 2.4 Det-mAP, and collapsing spatial structure before temporal modeling causes an additional 9.65 Det-mAP and 14.35 Seg-mAP drop on ATARS.
sgWkDEomPy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it poses a clear question about how long to preserve spatial structure, is well motivated for concurrent and trajectory-dependent actions, and shows consistent ablation evidence that pooling before class prediction hurts.
sgWkDEomPy.main_concern: Novelty is limited because it combines known components (ConvLSTM-style recurrent states, token-wise prediction with pooling), and baselines are not matched in representation since most receive pooled features while SpaTAD uses dense tokens.

bXff5a1ygV.one_liner: Scores pluralism in long-form responses with a rank-consistent lattice learned over a topic space from a gold corpus.
bXff5a1ygV.problem: Evaluating Overton pluralism in long-form LLM responses is hard because there is no well-defined Overton window, long text disrupts objective evaluation, and human-in-the-loop evaluation is costly and slow.
bXff5a1ygV.method: OvERALE projects individual human viewpoints (micro lens) into a topic-level domain (meso lens), trains a rank-consistent pluralism lattice over a static gold corpus, and uses it as a fixed reference to score new responses.
bXff5a1ygV.key_idea: Train a rank-consistent pluralism scoring field over a shared topic space built from human-written corpora, then score each response sentence against that fixed reference.
bXff5a1ygV.evidence: Perturbation sensitivity tests (including Philosophia-QA) and a human study, with a topic space built from five human-written datasets and evaluation on two independently sourced QA datasets.
bXff5a1ygV.claimed_gains: not stated in the visible abstract (reviews cite a correlation of 0.58 with human pluralism ratings and an ICC of 0.76 on a shared set of 50 responses).
bXff5a1ygV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating pluralism of long-form responses without costly human annotation is timely and important, and that the perturbation tests and human study give useful evidence.
bXff5a1ygV.main_concern: Conclusions go beyond the evidence because sentences are scored independently and averaged (ignoring relations and repetition) and training also favors the center of the topic space, so effects cannot be attributed to ranking supervision alone.

ecZKzihoAX.one_liner: Registers the comparator before scoring and applies exact binomial tests on training-run excess to refute virtual cell model reliability claims.
ecZKzihoAX.problem: Virtual cell predictors are judged by held-out accuracy, but their added value depends on the comparator's selection information and rule, which existing reliability tests take as given.
ecZKzihoAX.method: FalsifyVC indexes verdicts by comparator authority, separating the reliability threshold, margin, and run budget, and uses exact binomial tests to count training runs whose excess over the comparator clears a registered margin.
ecZKzihoAX.key_idea: Index each reliability verdict by a pre-registered comparator authority and test with an exact binomial test how many training runs beat that comparator by a registered margin.
ecZKzihoAX.evidence: Two Replogle screens with twelve fresh target splits each, an independent screen with thirty runs, a registered positive control, and fixed pseudobulk and per-target envelope comparators, applied to GEARS, STATE, and CPA.
ecZKzihoAX.claimed_gains: No GEARS run clears the margin against any comparator across twelve fresh target splits on two Replogle screens, and on an independent screen GEARS clears it in none of thirty runs while a registered positive control clears it in all thirty.
ecZKzihoAX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework pursues a valuable goal of reliable evaluation of perturbation predictors, is well written, and that follow-up experiments strengthen the negative result for GEARS, STATE, and CPA.
ecZKzihoAX.main_concern: The conceptual contribution is modest since comparator reporting and binomial run testing have precedents, and reviewers also question fit to the venue and the correlation-based score.

An4EXp1kt0.one_liner: Characterizes failure-to-settle in LLMs asked for nonexistent symbols and shows steering internals or output representations can control it.
An4EXp1kt0.problem: When asked for a nonexistent item such as the seahorse emoji, models can cycle through proposing, rejecting, and reconsidering nearby symbols instead of saying that no answer exists.
An4EXp1kt0.method: The authors define failure-to-settle, show it extends to rare-language vocabulary and scientific and standardized symbols, and intervene on model internals (steering along belief-in-existence and reasoning-persistence directions) and output representations (removing a valid output or constructing a synthetic output token). They also introduce a benchmark.
An4EXp1kt0.key_idea: Steer along directions for belief in an item's existence or reasoning persistence, or alter output-token availability, to control whether a model keeps searching or commits.
An4EXp1kt0.evidence: Multiple open-weight model families with steering, prompting, and vocabulary-level interventions and a new benchmark measuring the behavior.
An4EXp1kt0.claimed_gains: not stated in the abstract (a review cites commitment steering raising completed generations from 32.46% to 86.84%).
An4EXp1kt0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies an interesting, general failure mode and supports it with extensive intervention experiments across steering, prompting, and vocabulary-level changes.
An4EXp1kt0.main_concern: Scope is narrow because most results are emoji-based with little evidence for other symbol types or real-world tasks, and some synthetic-token controls are incomplete.

1LfPQOF3bZ.one_liner: Benchmark and probing study showing MLLMs retain conflicting visual information but fail to use or ignore it as instructed.
1LfPQOF3bZ.problem: It is unclear how reliably multimodal LLMs use or disregard an image that conflicts with prior knowledge when instructed, and whether failures come from missing visual information in the representations (H1) or from mishandling it (H2).
1LfPQOF3bZ.method: The WhatIfVis benchmark holds image and question fixed while changing only the instruction to use or ignore the image, across five conflict types. The analysis combines reconstruction models on final-layer image tokens, LoRA on the language backbone with a frozen vision encoder, activation patching, and a learned rank-1 intervention.
1LfPQOF3bZ.key_idea: Pair use-the-image and ignore-the-image instructions on the same example, then combine reconstruction probes, LoRA, patching, and rank-1 interventions to separate information retention from information use.
1LfPQOF3bZ.evidence: Six MLLMs on WhatIfVis, reconstruction from three frozen MLLMs, LoRA on one conflict type with transfer to four held-out types, activation patching, and transfer of a rank-1 intervention to the original model.
1LfPQOF3bZ.claimed_gains: Mean paired accuracy is only 14.1% across six MLLMs; LoRA on one conflict type raises it to 58.75%, and a learned rank-1 intervention reaches 34.2% on the adapter-free model without verbal intent instructions.
1LfPQOF3bZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paired benchmark and complementary analyses (reconstruction, probing, interventions) give useful evidence that MLLMs retain visual information yet fail to use it as instructed.
1LfPQOF3bZ.main_concern: Reviewers note the study mainly combines established techniques and that recoverability through a separately trained reconstruction model does not show the original MLLM can use the information.

d8SHoWPspO.one_liner: VLM reward model trained on 10k physics preference pairs writes rationales before scoring videos, for joint prompt and video RL.
d8SHoWPspO.problem: Video generators produce clips that violate basic physics, and prior RL methods use hand-designed verifiers that each check one property and are unreliable in open-world videos.
d8SHoWPspO.method: A physics preference dataset of 10k prompt-video pairs (25 sub-scenes in five categories) has labels known from how pairs are built, with annotator rationales scoring six physical dimensions and listing violations with time intervals and boxes. Phy-Judger, a VLM, writes a rationale before scoring, and a prompt policy trained jointly with the video policy rewrites prompts to add missing physical conditions.
d8SHoWPspO.key_idea: Learn the physics reward as a rationale-first VLM judge that ties scores to localized violations, and train a prompt-rewriting policy jointly with the video policy.
d8SHoWPspO.evidence: Joint RL on MiniMax-H3 evaluated with VBench-2.0 Physics, PhyWorldBench, and human comparisons, as described in the abstract and reviews.
d8SHoWPspO.claimed_gains: Joint RL with Phy-Judger raises the VBench-2.0 Physics score of MiniMax-H3 from 75.80 to 78.83 (the abstract is cut off after this); reviews also cite PhyWorldBench rising from 0.155 to 0.203 and human preference of 49.1% versus 33.1%.
d8SHoWPspO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a learned physics reward with localized explanations covers errors beyond hand-designed verifiers and that gains extend to independent benchmarks and human comparisons.
d8SHoWPspO.main_concern: Preference labels are assigned by construction and may reward source recognition rather than physics, and the visual grounding of the rationales is not directly validated.

sA8QZlj3mj.one_liner: Audits American English preference across LLM pretraining and post-training data, tokenizers, prediction cost, and generation using matched AmE-BrE variants.
sA8QZlj3mj.problem: Widely used platforms expose English (US) as the primary English setting, and it is unclear how American English becomes the default as a structural bias across the LLM pipeline.
