tSXGCumseL.main_concern: GAE is the only comparator, so simple alternatives such as lowering lambda near endpoints and the Daley et al. (2024) equicorrelation model are untested, and the theory assumes a fixed endpoint rather than random termination.

4xIH8SQ6iq.one_liner: Encodes observed geometry and appearance into the generative latent space as initialization (latent forcing) for faithful multi-view 3D mesh generation.
4xIH8SQ6iq.problem: 3D mesh generators treat observations as coarse conditioning, so generated geometry and appearance can deviate from the input views, and existing benchmarks poorly cover realistic scenes and occlusions.
4xIH8SQ6iq.method: FORGE3D replaces initial noise with latents encoded from observed geometry and appearance (latent forcing) on a pretrained generator, then finetunes with correspondence-aware multi-view attention. It also introduces FORGE3DBench, with more than 300 unique assets in simulated scenes.
4xIH8SQ6iq.key_idea: Initialize generation from latents obtained by passing observed 3D points and image evidence through the backbone's own encoders, instead of from pure noise.
4xIH8SQ6iq.evidence: Latent forcing applied to a pretrained generator without training, finetuning with multi-view attention, and evaluation on FORGE3DBench scenes with varied lighting, clutter, and occlusion.
4xIH8SQ6iq.claimed_gains: Latent forcing improves geometric fidelity without additional training and finetuning further improves appearance; no numbers visible in the abstract.
4xIH8SQ6iq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree observation faithfulness is a worthwhile problem, latent forcing is simple and helps even without training, and FORGE3DBench covers realistic clutter, lighting, and occlusion with calibrated views and annotations.
4xIH8SQ6iq.main_concern: Baseline comparisons may be unequal (the method uses depth input that baselines such as Hunyuan3D-2MV and Pixal3D lack), and the handling of unobserved geometry and the attention components is under-specified.

GmMTqK1Xwg.one_liner: A frozen LLM sets adaptive sub-goals and judges samples; its preferences are distilled into a flow generator with DPO.
GmMTqK1Xwg.problem: Aligning scientific generators to high-level natural-language goals is hard without an explicit proxy reward, and the initial generator may put negligible probability on designs satisfying the final goal.
GmMTqK1Xwg.method: In LLM-to-Flow Distillation, a frozen LLM acts as an adaptive teacher: given a goal, it builds a curriculum of sub-goals aware of the flow's current capabilities and judges sampled candidates each round. Those judgments induce preferences that are distilled into the generator through DPO.
GmMTqK1Xwg.key_idea: An LLM teacher picks sub-goals matched to the generator's current capability and judges samples, giving dense preference signals for DPO without a proxy reward.
GmMTqK1Xwg.evidence: Natural-language discovery goals (such as anticancer peptides) on peptide and molecule generators, with QM9 mentioned in reviews, compared against reward-based methods with held-out evaluators.
GmMTqK1Xwg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that steering generators with natural-language goals instead of proxy rewards is well motivated, and that the Goal 5 result, where a sparse reward fails but the adaptive curriculum succeeds, is clear evidence.
GmMTqK1Xwg.main_concern: Held-out evaluators are not independent of the LLM teacher or may overlap its training data, discovery claims rest on computational proxies, and design choices (number of rounds, seeds, a no-curriculum ablation) are underspecified.

hDLLRkfOGI.one_liner: Single-pass LiDAR scene completion that derives candidate placement, feature scales, and visibility supervision from each return's beam footprint.
hDLLRkfOGI.problem: Diffusion LiDAR completion needs many network evaluations per scan, and single-pass methods use hand-set rules for candidate points, feature scales, and visibility that are unrelated to how the sensor samples the scene.
hDLLRkfOGI.method: BeamScene uses a Beam-Footprint-Aware Candidate Constructor (bounded candidate budget proportional to footprint, tangent-plane spreading, immutable measured anchors), a Footprint-Aligned Shared-Scale Encoder (shared sparse kernels over eight voxel resolutions with a parameter-free gate), and a training-only Frustum-Ray Visibility Objective.
hDLLRkfOGI.key_idea: Compute each return's beam footprint from its range and the sensor's angular resolution, and use it to set candidate density, resolution weighting, and the visibility loss.
hDLLRkfOGI.evidence: SemanticKITTI voxel IoU at 0.2 m and 0.1 m against LiNeXt, with KITTI-360 evaluation without finetuning, ablations, and parameter and latency comparisons per reviews.
hDLLRkfOGI.claimed_gains: Raises SemanticKITTI voxel IoU at 0.2 m and 0.1 m from 19.45 and 6.30 (LiNeXt) to values truncated in the abstract (24.91 and 8.74 per a review).
hDLLRkfOGI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it improves completion over LiNeXt with fewer parameters and that the ablations support the components, with cross-dataset generalization to KITTI-360.
hDLLRkfOGI.main_concern: The contribution relative to LiNeXt is blurred, some component gains are marginal with many under-documented hyperparameters, and physical consistency is not directly validated given the coarse angular ray bins in the visibility objective.

WYOmlBVRse.one_liner: RegretBench measures whether coding agents back up state before destructive actions; BackUpper is a harness plug-in that backs up state.
WYOmlBVRse.problem: Coding agents complete tasks while modifying real-world state but rarely preserve state they may later need, and task completion does not imply backup awareness.
WYOmlBVRse.method: RegretBench provides 205 executable tasks grounded in user regret moments reported on X.com, GitHub and Stack Overflow. BackUpper is a harness plug-in layer that checks every tool call and preserves affected state before modification, combining rule-based strategies for common destructive operations with a lightweight subagent for complex cases.
WYOmlBVRse.key_idea: Intercept every tool call in the agent harness and snapshot affected state beforehand, using rules for common destructive operations and a subagent for complex ones.
WYOmlBVRse.evidence: 205 tasks run against real systems (e.g. PostgreSQL, GitLab and Reddit clones, an email server, Kubernetes) across six frontier models, with restoration-similarity, cost, and preference-aware backup measurements.
WYOmlBVRse.claimed_gains: Agents complete 86.1% of tasks but back up in only 15.2%; BackUpper restores state to 92.2% average similarity, covers every regret-moment action, costs $0.014 per task with 7x fewer tokens than main-agent self-backup, and reaches 84.5% F1 when users state preferences.
WYOmlBVRse.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the gap between task completion and recovery preparedness is practically meaningful and that the benchmark is grounded in real incidents, with a practical harness-agnostic plug-in.
WYOmlBVRse.main_concern: The 100% coverage and restoration claims rest on an LLM judge (humans confirmed 188 of 200 samples) and character-level snapshot similarity, and the benchmark cannot penalize unnecessary backups.

iyHrF9jVNT.one_liner: Hybrid attention replacing sliding windows with top-k block retrieval, pairing each block with a prefix state of its preceding context.
iyHrF9jVNT.problem: Hybrid linear and softmax architectures such as NHA restrict exact attention to a fixed local window, limiting retrieval of precise long-range evidence.
iyHrF9jVNT.method: PHBA uses top-k block-sparse retrieval and couples each retrieved block with a compact prefix state built by a gated linear recurrence at block boundaries, retrieved together with the token block in a unified layer. A hardware-aware Triton implementation streams routed blocks and prefix states without materializing large intermediate tensors.
iyHrF9jVNT.key_idea: Retrieve token blocks by content routing and attach to each a recurrent prefix-state snapshot of its preceding context, read jointly in one attention layer.
iyHrF9jVNT.evidence: Models up to 1.3B parameters trained from scratch and compared with MoBA, GSA, KDA and NHA on language modeling, commonsense tasks, NIAH, RULER and LongBench (per reviews).
iyHrF9jVNT.claimed_gains: Improves long-context and retrieval performance over strong linear and hybrid baselines while retaining efficient training and inference; no numbers are stated in the abstract.
iyHrF9jVNT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that pairing sparse block retrieval with recurrent memory is a coherent extension and shows gains on retrieval and language modeling against relevant baselines.
iyHrF9jVNT.main_concern: Novelty is limited relative to NHA plus MoBA routing, and no ablation isolates the prefix-state snapshots or validates long-context claims beyond the 8K training length.

jAtLnNKlsy.one_liner: Exact n^O(1/gamma^2) algorithm for training one ReLU under squared loss, parameterized by activation margin, with a matching ETH-based lower bound.
jAtLnNKlsy.problem: Training a single ReLU on n points is NP-hard and W[1]-hard in the input dimension d, so no phi(d) n^o(d) algorithm exists under the clique hypothesis.
jAtLnNKlsy.method: The paper defines the activation margin gamma of an optimal neuron and shows that if some optimum separates fired from unfired inputs with margin at least gamma, squared-loss training on rational data has a global minimizer computable in n^O(1/gamma^2) poly(L) time. A reduction shows margin-promised training is W[1]-hard in 1/gamma^2 with a matching exponent lower bound.
jAtLnNKlsy.key_idea: Count large-margin activation patterns (bounded in terms of 1/gamma^2) and solve a convex problem per pattern, making the exponent independent of dimension.
jAtLnNKlsy.evidence: Theory only: upper bound proofs, W[1]-hardness, and a lower bound under the same clique hypothesis, with no experiments.
jAtLnNKlsy.claimed_gains: Runtime n^O(1/gamma^2) poly(L) with exponent independent of d and optimal up to a constant factor, versus the phi(d) n^o(d) poly(L) barrier for dimension-parameterized training.
jAtLnNKlsy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives matching upper and lower bounds for a well-studied problem under a new margin parameter and that the results appear sound.
jAtLnNKlsy.main_concern: Technical novelty is limited because the bounds combine existing techniques, and the margin parameter is poorly motivated since d and 1/gamma are incomparable and the optimal margin cannot be computed efficiently.

yWaqs5qKnR.one_liner: Diagnostic hides the target molecule, defining it by a source molecule plus a structural edit, to test LLM chemical prediction.
yWaqs5qKnR.problem: Chemical benchmarks give the target's identity directly, so it is hard to tell whether LLM predictions come from structure-property reasoning or from memory and contextual cues.
yWaqs5qKnR.method: The Identity-Blinded Reasoning Diagnostic defines the target by a known source entity and an explicit structural edit, preserving the information needed to determine the target. Source labels can be supplied or replaced while the target, edit, and ground truth stay fixed.
yWaqs5qKnR.key_idea: Replace only the source entity's label while holding structure, edit, and target fixed, to measure how much predictions follow the supplied label rather than the chemistry.
yWaqs5qKnR.evidence: Six tasks spanning odor prediction, molecular property prediction, retrosynthesis, and reaction yield prediction, with a target-reconstruction check that succeeds 86-100% of the time per a reviewer.
yWaqs5qKnR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the fixed-target source-label interventions give direct evidence of source-label dependence and that hiding the target by source plus edit is a simple, applicable design.
yWaqs5qKnR.main_concern: Label-consistent and label-inconsistent groups are not matched for difficulty, and following a source label presented as fact may be legitimate reasoning, so results do not separate memorization from chemical reasoning.

mTLnhwOGaz.one_liner: Label-free, instance-specific test-time training that selects attention heads by intervention responses and adapts only those heads in frozen VLMs.
mTLnhwOGaz.problem: Existing test-time training predefines which model components to adapt, risking inefficient parameter updates and unnecessary model drift when test-time data are scarce.
mTLnhwOGaz.method: TTT-Head identifies tunable attention heads at the task and instance levels and performs sparse, instance-specific adaptation guided by label-free Head-Action responses, with baseline-anchored supervision to limit overcorrection.
mTLnhwOGaz.key_idea: Select heads whose single-head interventions raise an alternative answer's relative preference and train gates on those heads, since visual-evidence relevance does not imply adaptation eligibility.
mTLnhwOGaz.evidence: Seven VQA-style benchmarks covering visual reasoning, hallucination, multimodal perception, and OCR, across three VLM families at 7B and 13B scales.
mTLnhwOGaz.claimed_gains: TTT-Head consistently improves the frozen baselines across all evaluated VLMs, with an average gain of 2.65 points on the LLaVA-1.5-7B backbone.
mTLnhwOGaz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating visual-evidence heads from adaptation-eligible heads is a well-motivated problem and that gains are consistent across benchmarks and architectures, with helpful ablations.
mTLnhwOGaz.main_concern: Intervention support measures controllability rather than answer correctness, so it is unvalidated that stronger head support selects a more accurate alternative, and the method has many hyperparameters.

TeJQpaiiuJ.one_liner: Decoder reads register tokens together with all patch tokens, and an attention-pooling predictor recovers registers from generated patches for diffusion.
TeJQpaiiuJ.problem: Patch-based image decoders discard non-spatial register tokens that encode global scene properties such as illumination, blur, and style, leaving the decoder to recover appearance from patches alone.
TeJQpaiiuJ.method: Using representation autoencoders with frozen register-equipped encoders, the decoder processes four register tokens with all patch tokens through joint self-attention. For generation, a multi-head attention pooling (MHAP) predictor recovers register features from sampled patches without modifying the pretrained diffusion model.
TeJQpaiiuJ.key_idea: Feed the encoder's register tokens to the decoder through joint self-attention, and predict them from generated patches with attention pooling for generation.
TeJQpaiiuJ.evidence: ImageNet-1K reconstruction with DINOv2 and DINOv3 ViT-B decoders, appearance probes, paired reconstruction-error analysis, fixed-decoder register substitutions, and transfer to NINCO and Places365 per a reviewer.
TeJQpaiiuJ.claimed_gains: On ImageNet-1K, ViT-B decoders reach mean reconstruction FIDs of 0.472 with DINOv2 and 0.442 with DINOv3, reductions of 9.5% and 5.2% over patch-only baselines, with PSNRs of 19.73 and 20.54 dB.
TeJQpaiiuJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the research question is concrete and the reconstruction gains are consistent, supported by careful controls such as shuffled and mean registers, learned tokens, and multi-seed paired statistics.
TeJQpaiiuJ.main_concern: The conceptual advance is limited since registers are known to carry global information, and ablations do not clearly separate register decoding from using the CLS token or an extra learned readout.

AtlLlKy9n8.one_liner: splitDGD enforces baseline-versus-perturbation decoupling architecturally with two latent blocks, masking the condition block for control cells.
AtlLlKy9n8.problem: Decoupling normal cellular state from perturbation response is hard without leaking condition information into the invariant component or degrading representation utility, which existing variational methods with soft regularisers or structural constraints fail to avoid.
AtlLlKy9n8.method: An extension of the Deep Generative Decoder with two separate latent blocks, an invariant block for condition-independent variation and a condition-specific block for the perturbation response, with the latter masked when the perturbation is absent.
AtlLlKy9n8.key_idea: Build two separate latent blocks and mask the condition-specific block for unperturbed samples, so decoupling is enforced by architecture rather than soft regularisation.
AtlLlKy9n8.evidence: Controlled image benchmarks and single-cell perturbation datasets (reviews mention Kang and Haber), in unsupervised and label-supervised regimes, measuring condition leakage against representation utility.
AtlLlKy9n8.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract only claims splitDGD is the only method to mitigate the leakage-versus-utility tradeoff.
AtlLlKy9n8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is clear and important and that fitting the baseline prior from controls with control masking is a simple, well-motivated design that needs no adversarial training.
AtlLlKy9n8.main_concern: Novelty and attribution are unclear: the method largely combines the DGD framework with the zeroing-out used in contrastive analysis (similar to multiDGD), and missing ablations and baselines such as biolord leave the source of gains unclear.

sExnSJkndM.one_liner: Splits counted behavior change after post-training into propensity and reach by teacher-forcing the predecessor on successor responses.
sExnSJkndM.problem: Counted changes in a behavior (e.g., "delve", "wait") after post-training mix a change in what the model does in the same context with a change in which contexts it reaches.
sExnSJkndM.method: Teacher-force the predecessor model on the successor's responses to split the counted change exactly into a propensity term and a reach term. They apply the split to released model pairs and to fixes that set the successor's behavior probability to the predecessor's.
sExnSJkndM.key_idea: Scoring the successor's own trajectories under the predecessor yields an exact additive split of a counted behavior change into propensity and reach terms.
sExnSJkndM.evidence: Released post-training model pairs (10 transitions across 8 model families per reviews), an Olmo-3 RL-on-code case study with "However" openers, and five intervention cases of a probability-matching fix.
sExnSJkndM.claimed_gains: The split predicts correctly in all five checked cases whether a fix narrows or widens the count gap; propensity and reach shares vary widely and can have opposite signs.
sExnSJkndM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the decomposition clear, assumption-free and cheap to compute, and note that opposite-sign cases show raw counts can mislead.
sExnSJkndM.main_concern: The practical payoff is unclear (how the split guides fixes or model improvement), and propensity values can change sign with the reference or setup choice.

zJTByJexQ4.one_liner: Training-free closed-form projections on denoised coordinates fix steric clashes and ligand geometry in AlphaFold 3-style diffusion samplers.
zJTByJexQ4.problem: AF3-style cofolding outputs are often physically invalid (chain overlaps, distorted ligand bonds and angles, non-planar rings, inverted stereocentres), and existing fixes via guided sampling or fine-tuning are costly or architecture-specific.
zJTByJexQ4.method: Two closed-form, local, displacement-capped projection operators act on the denoised clean-coordinate estimate x0-hat: an inter-chain van der Waals projection that pushes apart clashing atoms, and a ligand distance-geometry projection that restores bond lengths, angles, contacts, planarity and chirality. They need no network evaluations, gradients, or weight changes.
zJTByJexQ4.key_idea: Because physical validity is checkable at inference time, project the denoised coordinate estimate onto valid geometry with sparse closed-form operators at late diffusion steps.
zJTByJexQ4.evidence: Two independently developed models (Boltz-2 and OpenFold-3 per reviews) on five benchmark sets, with ablations on when the corrections are applied and comparisons with post-hoc correction.
zJTByJexQ4.claimed_gains: Recovers perfect AlphaFold 3 physical validity across five benchmarks with no measurable loss in structural accuracy and negligible added runtime and memory overhead.
zJTByJexQ4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a lightweight training-free fix with no extra denoiser evaluations that raises validity with little change in accuracy or cost on two models.
zJTByJexQ4.main_concern: Related methods (Gauss-Seidel Projection, PhysDock) are not compared or discussed, and the 100% validity uses a best-of-five oracle that does not show per-sample validity.

HGxmIPIXBk.one_liner: Evaluates six EEG foundation models under test-time perturbations, attribution analysis and probing to look beyond clean accuracy.
HGxmIPIXBk.problem: EEG foundation models are evaluated mostly on clean in-distribution accuracy, which shows modest gains over supervised baselines and weak frozen representations.
HGxmIPIXBk.method: Evaluates six EEG foundation models and a supervised baseline across ten datasets in three layers: robustness to noise and channel dropout, attribution-based interpretability, and expressiveness via pooling strategy comparison, block-wise probing and attention analysis.
HGxmIPIXBk.key_idea: Preserving token-level embeddings instead of pooling them recovers frozen-head performance, indicating poor head-only results stem from pooling and not from weak representations.
HGxmIPIXBk.evidence: Six EEG foundation models plus a supervised baseline on ten datasets with additive noise, random and region-based channel dropout, attribution methods, and block-wise probing and attention analysis on REVE and NeuroRVQ per reviews.
HGxmIPIXBk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the analysis is timely and useful, exposing failure modes clean accuracy misses (such as channel removal versus zero-padding) and showing the importance of output aggregation.
HGxmIPIXBk.main_concern: Controls are not strong enough: perturbations are synthetic only, noise bandwidth is unmatched across models, one dropout mask is reused across folds, common average referencing may put inputs out of distribution, and block-wise analyses cover only two models.

gi7YJ6fYnd.one_liner: Feeds critic features, trained on the full replay buffer, into the preference reward model to reduce overfitting to few labels.
gi7YJ6fYnd.problem: In preference-based RL, the reward model must generalize from a few hundred labeled preference trajectories to millions of visited state-action pairs and overfits the labeled data.
gi7YJ6fYnd.method: BRM copies the features of the critic, which is trained on the full replay buffer, and uses them as input to the reward model trained on only a few hundred labeled preferences. Reviewers add that it uses a skip connection, ensemble heads, and per-round reinitialization.
gi7YJ6fYnd.key_idea: Reuse the critic's replay-buffer-trained features as inputs to the reward model so it starts from a representation learned on far more data than the preference labels.
gi7YJ6fYnd.evidence: Twelve tasks from DeepMind Control Suite and MetaWorld against seven PbRL baselines; reviewers note ten seeds, three backbones, and control ablations with random features, actor features, and larger raw-input networks.
gi7YJ6fYnd.claimed_gains: Task-normalized IQM of 0.85 versus 0.55 for the strongest of seven PbRL baselines.
gi7YJ6fYnd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree BRM gets substantial gains from a simple change that reuses an existing critic, supported by broad experiments and careful control ablations.
gi7YJ6fYnd.main_concern: The closest related method, REED, is missing from the seven baselines, and the headline gap against QPA also mixes ensemble size and augmentation differences.

a0ZOniNXXB.one_liner: Solver-certified single-premise edits test whether answers track decisive changes while remaining consistent across presentation contexts.
a0ZOniNXXB.problem: Isolated answer accuracy can hide failures to distinguish minimally different problems whose correct answers change.
a0ZOniNXXB.method: OETW creates sibling constraint problems differing in one premise and certifies their answer multiplicities with a solver. Verified accuracy requires correct premise-sensitive answers across separate and grouped presentations.
a0ZOniNXXB.key_idea: Score single-premise sibling problems jointly for answer changes and consistency across isolated, joint, and pairwise views.
a0ZOniNXXB.evidence: The benchmark evaluates seven models on 1,200 triads from three constraint families with solver certification, byte-identity checks, and surface-feature controls.
a0ZOniNXXB.claimed_gains: As problems grow, reported raw accuracy falls to 33% and verified accuracy to 2%.
a0ZOniNXXB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate solver-certified minimal edits and controls that expose reasoning failures hidden by ordinary accuracy.
a0ZOniNXXB.main_concern: Multiple reviewers question whether the raw-to-verified accuracy gap isolates premise tracking rather than context, budget, or elicitation-format difficulties.

Oix3W4XCvH.one_liner: Orthogonal residual tests recover a shared causal order and detect parent-set changes across environments.
Oix3W4XCvH.problem: Detecting a changed causal mechanism does not establish that the underlying causal graph has changed.
Oix3W4XCvH.method: STORM estimates a common order by repeatedly removing nodes without children across environments, then tests whether omitting candidate parents changes conditional means. Orthogonal scores reduce first-order sensitivity to regression errors.
Oix3W4XCvH.key_idea: Combine shared-order recovery with parent-omission conditional-mean tests whose orthogonal scores suppress first-order regression-estimation errors.
Oix3W4XCvH.evidence: Identifiability results for nonlinear additive noise models accompany synthetic and real-world experiments and orthogonal-score ablations.
Oix3W4XCvH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the relevance of causal structure-shift detection and the theoretical analysis supporting the approach.
Oix3W4XCvH.main_concern: Multiple reviewers request comparisons with learning each environment's graph separately to establish the advantage of shared-order estimation.

GGbI4BLTNN.one_liner: Global and patch-level DINOv3 feature alignment pretrains recurrent event encoders using synchronized RGB-event streams without labels.
GGbI4BLTNN.problem: Scarce event labels and costly pretraining limit foundation-model transfer to event-native recurrent detection backbones.
GGbI4BLTNN.method: A frozen DINOv3 teacher processes RGB frames while an RVT-plus-DINOv3 student processes events. Cosine alignment and patch-level InfoNCE transfer features, after which the RGB branch is discarded.
GGbI4BLTNN.key_idea: Align recurrent event-stream features with synchronized frozen RGB-teacher global and patch features using cosine and contrastive losses.
GGbI4BLTNN.evidence: Pretraining uses DSEC, with downstream DSEC-Detection, DSEC-Semantic, and GEN1 detection evaluations.
GGbI4BLTNN.claimed_gains: Pretraining takes 7k steps, 9 A6000 GPU-hours, and 1.2 EFLOPs, with 2.7× and 26× fewer FLOPs than GEP and TESPEC, while DSEC-Detection reaches 46.3 mAP versus 38.4 from scratch (+7.9).
GGbI4BLTNN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate simple, efficient RGB-to-event representation transfer and encouraging downstream results.
GGbI4BLTNN.main_concern: Reviewers find limited cross-dataset generalization evidence, especially because the full model underperforms RVT baselines on GEN1.

9URsbc17T5.one_liner: Paired surface-attribute interventions identify shared judge biases for attenuation and calibrated LLM-panel aggregation.
9URsbc17T5.problem: Agreement among LLM judges can reflect shared presentation biases that observational scores cannot distinguish from target quality.
9URsbc17T5.method: VoirDire changes specified surface attributes while aiming to preserve evaluation targets and identifies nuisance-sensitive directions from paired score differences. It attenuates those directions and selects weights balancing item variation against intervention sensitivity.
9URsbc17T5.key_idea: Use paired intervention-induced score differences to identify and suppress nuisance-sensitive directions before aggregating judge outputs.
9URsbc17T5.evidence: Theoretical identification analysis and experiments on 12 datasets cover continuous scoring, binary classification, and pairwise preference.
9URsbc17T5.claimed_gains: VoirDire reduces MAE by up to 46.6% on continuous-score tasks relative to existing LLM-judge aggregation baselines.
9URsbc17T5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value paired interventions as an interpretable source of information about shared judge biases and the diverse evaluation.
9URsbc17T5.main_concern: Multiple reviewers flag possible label reuse across random splits during configuration selection and request an untouched or nested test evaluation.

y0RrYUKddd.one_liner: Corpus-trained neural memories condition frozen retriever query embeddings and amortize adaptation across subsequent queries.
y0RrYUKddd.problem: Fixed dense embeddings cannot adapt to user- or corpus-specific semantics after deployment.
y0RrYUKddd.method: TTT-Retrieval augments a frozen embedding model with compact meta-trained memory modules. Self-supervised corpus writes update these memories, which then condition query embeddings during repeated reads.
y0RrYUKddd.key_idea: Write unlabeled corpus context into persistent neural memories and read those memories to contextualize query embeddings.
y0RrYUKddd.evidence: Experiments compare retrieval on LoCoMo, QASPER, and HotpotQA against frozen embeddings, supervised fine-tuning, and reranking approaches.
y0RrYUKddd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful corpus-specific adaptation, reusable memory across queries, and consistent retrieval improvements.
y0RrYUKddd.main_concern: Multiple reviewers note missing no-write and unrelated-corpus controls that would isolate test-time adaptation from meta-training and extra memory parameters.

UHtBTP1FWq.one_liner: Permutation-aware simplicial representations guide agent networks and world-model imagination in value-based multi-agent reinforcement learning.
UHtBTP1FWq.problem: Multi-agent learning needs representations that transfer across team compositions while supporting sample-efficient world-model training.
UHtBTP1FWq.method: The framework builds agent representations with permutation-invariant and equivariant structure and constrains embeddings to products of probability simplices. A similarly structured world model provides imagined trajectories to the mixing network.
UHtBTP1FWq.key_idea: Constrain agent and world-model latents to probability simplices within permutation-aware networks and feed imagined trajectories to the centralized mixer.
UHtBTP1FWq.evidence: Experiments cover SMAC, SMACv2, and MAMuJoCo with seven component ablations, design-space studies, and representation analyses.
UHtBTP1FWq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the representation design and extensive evaluation across benchmarks and architectural choices.
UHtBTP1FWq.main_concern: Multiple reviewers find the mathematical presentation unclear or inconsistent, making the architecture and training objectives difficult to verify.

gPis4lhWxe.one_liner: A logarithmically capped spectral potential proves fixed-width LinUCB achieves sublinear regret on curved action sets.
gPis4lhWxe.problem: Classical LinUCB regret guarantees require statistically valid confidence sets that grow with dimension and horizon to ensure optimism.
gPis4lhWxe.method: The authors analyze alpha-LinUCB with any fixed exploration width alpha > 0 on M-smooth, m-strongly convex action sets by introducing a logarithmically capped spectral potential that bounds contributions from well-explored directions to lower-bound the design matrix's smallest eigenvalue.
gPis4lhWxe.key_idea: Use a logarithmically capped spectral potential on smooth, strongly convex action sets to lower-bound design-matrix eigenvalues under fixed-width LinUCB exploration.
gPis4lhWxe.evidence: High-probability spectral and regret bounds are derived for smooth, strongly convex action sets and accompanied by a synthetic linear-bandit experiment.
gPis4lhWxe.claimed_gains: At the standard confidence width α ≍ √(d log T), the T-round regret bound in d dimensions is O((M/m) d √(T log T)) up to iterated-logarithmic factors, improving the classical LinUCB horizon dependence by a factor of √(log T).
gPis4lhWxe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that questioning the necessity of valid confidence sets in LinUCB is a compelling theoretical perspective and commend the explicit smallest-eigenvalue and sharpened regret bounds.
gPis4lhWxe.main_concern: Reviewers note restrictive smooth and strongly convex action-set assumptions that exclude polytopes, incremental novelty relative to Abeille et al. (2025), and a remaining √(log T) gap to the minimax lower bound.

irbGCY3OGO.one_liner: Heterogeneous graph policies refine feasible VNF deployments through exactly checked move-swap actions and best-incumbent retention.
irbGCY3OGO.problem: One-shot VNF migration constructors can leave inefficient placements or unresolved overload under interacting resource and delay constraints.
irbGCY3OGO.method: CORA first repairs and admits strictly feasible deployments, then encodes physical machines, VNF instances, and service chains as a heterogeneous graph. Learned search uses constraint-filtered moves and swaps while preserving the best feasible incumbent.
irbGCY3OGO.key_idea: Separate learned move-swap selection from exact feasibility checks and retain the best incumbent throughout refinement.
irbGCY3OGO.evidence: Evaluation uses 30 frozen fat-tree-8 test instances across three migration regimes, multiple starting-solution providers, and classical search baselines.
irbGCY3OGO.claimed_gains: CORA improves 20/29 (69.0%) paired feasible MSH-OR starts and 26/27 (96.3%) paired feasible MAT-GNN starts, with no paired degradation.
irbGCY3OGO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating construction, repair, and learned refinement while explicitly preserving modeled feasibility.
irbGCY3OGO.main_concern: Reviewers find the contribution of learned components insufficiently isolated from simpler refinement approaches.

fSC9jzrkmT.one_liner: Instance-level memory adaptation amortizes variational EM into recursive reasoning that can run without target observations.
fSC9jzrkmT.problem: The computational roles of persistent state, shared transformations, and local truncated-gradient supervision in recursive reasoners remain unclear.
fSC9jzrkmT.method: The framework adds an instance-level M-step that adapts memory conditioning the prior while shared weights stay fixed. Variational Autoreasoners learn local variational objectives and use a recursive prior for target-free execution.
fSC9jzrkmT.key_idea: Adapt per-problem memory to fit the prior to posterior explanations, then amortize inference and adaptation with local variational objectives.
fSC9jzrkmT.evidence: The paper establishes monotone likelihood ascent for ideal EM updates and decomposes posterior-versus-prior execution divergence into local KL terms.
fSC9jzrkmT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the EM interpretation and persistent-memory prior adaptation conceptually useful.
fSC9jzrkmT.main_concern: Reviewers find the connection between exact EM updates and the learned adapter insufficiently explained, especially without an amortized monotonicity guarantee.

RYUiZagmQM.one_liner: Per-group image coresets replace single feature-space targets in fairness-aware dataset distillation to incorporate within-group geometry.
RYUiZagmQM.problem: Single-vector class targets can match group means while ignoring within-group variation in fixed feature spaces.
RYUiZagmQM.method: The paper decomposes groupwise Bures-Wasserstein distance into centroid and covariance terms. Fair Geometric Distillation replaces point targets with per-group real-image coresets under a balanced budget.
RYUiZagmQM.key_idea: Distill against sets of group-specific real representatives instead of one feature-space point per class.
RYUiZagmQM.evidence: Fixed-feature analysis and experiments across six benchmarks assess groupwise Wasserstein error, fairness, and controls for variance, sampling, and coreset selection.
RYUiZagmQM.claimed_gains: At one fixed regularisation setting, FGD attains the lowest per-group Wasserstein error on all six benchmarks.
RYUiZagmQM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the focus on within-group geometry and the accompanying geometric diagnostics and fairness evaluation.
RYUiZagmQM.main_concern: Reviewers agree the proposed matching loss does not ensure medoid coverage or covariance preservation, weakening its geometric justification.

3N6YHQlPlv.one_liner: Outcome-supervised candidate scoring triggers bounded extra search and allocates computation in world-model planning.
3N6YHQlPlv.problem: Selecting the best imagined plan does not establish that it will succeed or that further search is worthwhile.
3N6YHQlPlv.method: StopTheDream links candidate actions to predicted consequences and grounds comparison scores in observed actions and outcomes. A learned allocator and bounded additional-search mechanism determine when to search further or act.
3N6YHQlPlv.key_idea: Use execution-grounded candidate success scores to compare plans and trigger bounded additional search.
3N6YHQlPlv.evidence: Experiments use 120 hierarchical world-model maze tasks and 1,000 CAST visual trajectories with planning-quality and computation measurements.
3N6YHQlPlv.claimed_gains: StopTheDream solves 117 versus CoVO-MPC's 113 tasks with 48.58% fewer latent transitions and 24.38% less planning time, and achieves 1.3629 absolute trajectory error, 4.18% below a locally trained PiJEPA baseline, with 54.11% fewer predictor calls.
3N6YHQlPlv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value outcome-grounded candidate comparison and the reported trade-off between planning quality and computation.
3N6YHQlPlv.main_concern: Reviewers find the common search-allocation procedure and its task-specific implementations insufficiently clear.

pCVWEYsqa1.one_liner: Geometry-derived pairwise temperatures soften uncertain contrastive similarities using learned per-view scales.
pCVWEYsqa1.problem: Deterministic similarity scores can overconfidently optimize ambiguous pairs, while earlier uncertainty methods neglect how representation noise affects pairwise similarity.
pCVWEYsqa1.method: DistCLR augments the global InfoNCE temperature with a pair-specific term shaped like similarity variance under representation noise. Learned per-view scales set its magnitude without Monte Carlo sampling or changes to the contrastive framework.
pCVWEYsqa1.key_idea: Propagate representation-noise geometry into pair-specific similarity temperatures whose magnitudes depend on learned view-hardness scales.
pCVWEYsqa1.evidence: Reviews describe multi-seed tests across contrastive frameworks and datasets including ImageNet-1k, plus transfer and open-set evaluations.
pCVWEYsqa1.claimed_gains: DistCLR adds less than 1% wall-clock overhead.
pCVWEYsqa1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the low-overhead integration of pair-specific uncertainty into existing contrastive learning frameworks.
pCVWEYsqa1.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the surrogate objective and variance assumptions justify the claimed probabilistic uncertainty interpretation.

tSTdpsm63c.one_liner: Laplacian PCA uses spatial structure to expose dense-feature components obscured by conventional RGB PCA visualizations.
tSTdpsm63c.problem: Standard PCA visualizations can misrepresent dense-feature quality through noise or excessive spatial smoothness.
tSTdpsm63c.method: The method incorporates a Laplace-operator-based spatial term into linear feature visualization. It identifies less noisy components and examines spatial bias in DINOv3 while preserving tokenwise linear projection.
tSTdpsm63c.key_idea: Add spatial structure through a Laplacian term when choosing linear components for dense-feature visualization.
tSTdpsm63c.evidence: Qualitative comparisons include DINOv3 and Perception Encoder, while quantitative tests assess alignment with semantic-segmentation and monocular-depth dimensions.
tSTdpsm63c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value showing that familiar PCA visualizations can misrepresent the spatial and semantic structure of dense features.
tSTdpsm63c.main_concern: Reviewers find limited methodological novelty relative to earlier spatially regularized dimensionality-reduction methods.

7rJzbhjSJt.one_liner: Branched spatial-relation queries test whether language models preserve unspoken arrangements consistently across query orders.
7rJzbhjSJt.problem: It remains unclear whether language models can maintain stable object relations internally without writing them in reasoning text.
7rJzbhjSJt.method: The evaluation separates thought privacy, self-consistency, and cross-order agreement using shared-prefix query branches. An extended Jacobian lens examines hidden-state alignment with object and direction words.
7rJzbhjSJt.key_idea: Branch a shared prefix into differently ordered relation queries to test commitment to one unspoken object arrangement.
7rJzbhjSJt.evidence: The abstract reports 15 models from 1B to 744B parameters, including standard and looped transformers, and Jacobian-lens analysis of Qwen3.8-27B.
7rJzbhjSJt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing thought privacy, within-branch consistency, and agreement across query orders.
7rJzbhjSJt.main_concern: Reviewers question whether the evaluation and internal probes justify claims about absent hidden memory.

Ts9bZceJ5W.one_liner: Bounded edits create matched benign-malicious agent trajectories for monitor training and feedback-guided data collection.
Ts9bZceJ5W.problem: Separately collected benign and malicious trajectories differ throughout execution, confounding monitor training and evaluation.
Ts9bZceJ5W.method: An adversarial editor inserts malicious side-task actions into real benign trajectories through bounded local edits. Mechanical checks and behavioral judges assess validity, while monitor feedback directs further collection.
Ts9bZceJ5W.key_idea: Construct malicious twins by locally editing benign trajectories while retaining their surrounding task context.
Ts9bZceJ5W.evidence: Experiments include external CUA-SHADE-Arena evaluation, trajectory and prefix diagnostics, and a four-round matched-training-size collection study.
Ts9bZceJ5W.claimed_gains: Direct training raises Qwen3.5-35B-A3B AUROC from 0.665 to 0.866 versus 0.753 with STRIDE and Gloom alone, while feedback-guided collection reaches 0.881 versus 0.770 for random collection.
Ts9bZceJ5W.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value controlled malicious-example construction and evidence of useful monitor training beyond the synthetic dataset.
Ts9bZceJ5W.main_concern: Reviewers find the specific benefit of minimal editing and pairing insufficiently separated from filtering, data volume, and feedback-driven collection.

hfK2z6l8yj.one_liner: Local participation history, loss references, and neighbor disagreement reweight decentralized language-model updates to reduce participation imbalance.
hfK2z6l8yj.problem: Loss-dependent participation can leave poorly performing nodes underrepresented and reinforce their high losses.
hfK2z6l8yj.method: RUMOR reweights updates using recent participation history and caps amplification with past local loss. Disagreement with active neighbors supplies an additional update-weight signal without requiring global statistics.
hfK2z6l8yj.key_idea: Combine participation-based reweighting with a local-loss cap and neighbor-model disagreement to adjust decentralized updates.
hfK2z6l8yj.evidence: Experiments evaluate a small transformer and seven pretrained models up to 12 billion parameters under loss-adaptive and fixed participation probabilities.
hfK2z6l8yj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the participation-performance feedback problem interesting and appreciate a correction based on locally available information.
hfK2z6l8yj.main_concern: Reviewers question how well the controlled loss-dependent participation setup represents real decentralized learning.

1XrWdM6GS0.one_liner: Transport-compatible endpoint couplings generalize discrete adjoint matching, with fiberwise marginalization producing an exact lower-variance controller target.
1XrWdM6GS0.problem: Translation-based discrete adjoint matching relies on additive reference dynamics and deterministic cyclic endpoint correspondences that need not be available.
1XrWdM6GS0.method: Transport Adjoint Matching derives an exact optimal-control potential-ratio identity using couplings between reference endpoint kernels. Under a shared-fiber marginal condition, Rao-Blackwellization removes auxiliary transport and endpoint randomness without constructing explicit transport matrices.
1XrWdM6GS0.key_idea: Marginalize auxiliary transport choices and local endpoint symbols within compatible reference-kernel fibers to compute the adjoint controller target.
1XrWdM6GS0.evidence: Theoretical identities and variance ordering accompany Ising and Potts experiments across three temperature regimes, including a larger Ising lattice and comparisons with DASBS.
1XrWdM6GS0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the exact controller-target derivation and its practical lower-variance implementation within discrete adjoint matching.
1XrWdM6GS0.main_concern: The change beyond DASBS appears limited to the controller target, and the broader conceptual and practical advantage remains insufficiently established.

WIVg3A3mBq.one_liner: Learned nonnegative test-row/training-row scores selectively reshape attention and prune uninformative context in tabular foundation models.
WIVg3A3mBq.problem: Temperature scaling trades off tail suppression against informative-row coverage, while nearest-neighbor retrieval uses similarity as a proxy for model attention.
WIVg3A3mBq.method: Tabular Selective Attention learns pairwise nonnegative scores to favor informative training rows without uniformly sharpening the attention distribution. The same scores support pruning context rows for faster inference.
WIVg3A3mBq.key_idea: Apply learned query-specific row scores to suppress uninformative context while retaining attention across the informative set.
WIVg3A3mBq.evidence: A temperature-scaling tradeoff analysis accompanies TabArena experiments on TabICLv2 and TabDPT, including attention behavior and pruning-efficiency evaluations.
WIVg3A3mBq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value selective row suppression and the evaluation across tabular architectures, with theoretical analysis of temperature scaling.
WIVg3A3mBq.main_concern: The assumed separation between informative and uninformative rows, including exact suppression properties, lacks sufficient practical validation.

UGftJlN2a5.one_liner: Semantic attention reliability and optimal-transport evidence mismatch jointly detect object hallucinations from decoder-layer trajectories.
UGftJlN2a5.problem: Visual-support detectors underexplore whether subsequent semantic updates remain consistent with the evidence selected by attention.
UGftJlN2a5.method: SAM recalibrates source-level attention writes using target-semantic support and compares FFN-induced visual preference with target-conditioned attention evidence through a state-calibrated optimal-transport score. A lightweight detector combines both signals across layers without changing the LVLM or its decoding.
UGftJlN2a5.key_idea: Combine semantically calibrated visual writes with the mismatch between attention-selected evidence and FFN-induced visual preferences.
UGftJlN2a5.evidence: Four LVLMs undergo MS COCO captioning and CLEVR and AMBER question-answering evaluations, with component ablations, layer analyses, and sensitivity tests.
UGftJlN2a5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value combining visual support with FFN-update information and the ablations showing complementary signals.
UGftJlN2a5.main_concern: The added complexity of the specific reliability and optimal-transport formulations lacks sufficient comparison with simpler combinations of the same underlying features.

k1nvp4AWYX.one_liner: Illumination-conditioned feature adaptation and geometry-guided completion recover indoor occupancy across normal and low lighting.
k1nvp4AWYX.problem: RGB occupancy prediction degrades in low light, while mixed-light training can reduce normal-light accuracy and leave missing occupied structure.
k1nvp4AWYX.method: DarkOcc learns illumination-robust features through Multi-Level Feature Adaptation. Geometry-guided occupancy completion combines these features with base depth and voxel predictions to recover missing structure.
k1nvp4AWYX.key_idea: Adapt visual features to illumination and fuse them with base geometry to complete missing occupied voxels.
k1nvp4AWYX.evidence: Experiments cover Occ-ScanNet-mini, embodied occupancy prediction, and a newly constructed real-world indoor benchmark spanning normal and low illumination.
k1nvp4AWYX.claimed_gains: DarkOcc improves Geo-IoU over MLA by 5.57 percentage points under severe low light and 5.13 pp under normal illumination on Occ-ScanNet-mini, and by 9.76 pp under low illumination on the real-world benchmark.
k1nvp4AWYX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that low-light indoor occupancy is a practically relevant problem and that illumination-induced incompleteness provides useful motivation.
k1nvp4AWYX.main_concern: The experiments do not sufficiently establish that the adaptation and completion modules address illumination-specific failures rather than providing generic refinement.

VLMVwDLU6q.one_liner: An anchored, branched equivariant transformer tests how anatomical orientation and canonical alignment affect neural fluid-surrogate accuracy.
VLMVwDLU6q.problem: The practical accuracy benefit of explicit equivariance may depend on boundary conditions, prediction targets, and orientation distributions.
VLMVwDLU6q.method: AB-GATr combines anchoring and branching with an E(3)-equivariant geometric algebra transformer to predict surface and volume quantities. The study compares equivariant and non-equivariant surrogates under canonical alignment and rotational augmentation.
VLMVwDLU6q.key_idea: Use an E(3)-equivariant anchored and branched surrogate while varying training and test orientations to examine alignment-dependent benefits.
VLMVwDLU6q.evidence: Three hemodynamic benchmarks and controlled ShapeNet-Car rotations compare AB-GATr with LaB-GATr, AB-UPT, and Transolver++ variants with and without rotational augmentation.
VLMVwDLU6q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value separating equation symmetry, full-problem symmetry, and data alignment when assessing equivariance across fluid-surrogate experiments.
VLMVwDLU6q.main_concern: Differences in parameters, representations, and normalization prevent the comparisons from fully isolating equivariance and canonical alignment as causes of the gains.

Is6x1cdPAa.one_liner: Local Rényi-entropy maximization removes targeted influence from the final federated model without retaining training history.
Is6x1cdPAa.problem: Federated unlearning often requires costly retraining, historical model storage, or recovery rounds involving clients that did not request deletion.
Is6x1cdPAa.method: FedRUn starts from the final global model and performs a Rényi-entropy-based unlearning objective locally at the requesting client. The design avoids stored historical updates and repeated recovery communication with other clients.
Is6x1cdPAa.key_idea: Optimize a Rényi-entropy forgetting objective at the requesting client directly from the final global model.
Is6x1cdPAa.evidence: Experiments cover multiple unlearning granularities and IID and non-IID settings, with runtime, forget-set accuracy, and membership-inference measurements.
Is6x1cdPAa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that client-side optimization reduces computation, communication, and historical-storage requirements across several unlearning settings.
Is6x1cdPAa.main_concern: Missing matched comparisons with Shannon entropy or uniform-target objectives leave the specific benefit of Rényi entropy unclear.

H90Ozokucr.one_liner: Controlled computation and continuation tasks diagnose multilingual reasoning failures and motivate ordered arithmetic-state supervision before chain-of-thought training.
H90Ozokucr.problem: Final-answer accuracy cannot distinguish multilingual calculation failures from failures to identify inputs, choose operations, or continue a solution.
H90Ozokucr.method: The framework separately tests autonomous solving, computation of supplied operations, and continuation from correct partial solutions while controlling cross-language correspondence. Guided by those diagnostics, Qwen3.5-4B trains first on ordered arithmetic steps and then on full target-language chain-of-thought.
H90Ozokucr.key_idea: Separate access to required arithmetic states from executing them, then teach ordered arithmetic states before full natural-language reasoning.
H90Ozokucr.evidence: Synthetic-language and English-Chinese experiments cover two open-source model families, with matched-exposure Qwen3.5-4B training and Swahili and Bengali MGSM evaluations.
H90Ozokucr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating autonomous solving, conditional computation, and continuation provides a clearer diagnosis than final-answer accuracy alone.
H90Ozokucr.main_concern: The small training gains have seed-level confidence intervals crossing zero, leaving their reliability uncertain.

FH6pNJfJ8c.one_liner: Hierarchical reasoning queries and multiple annotators evaluate how video summaries change with user intent.
FH6pNJfJ8c.problem: Existing video-summarization benchmarks often test generic importance or simple retrieval rather than intent-sensitive temporal, semantic, and knowledge-based reasoning.
FH6pNJfJ8c.method: SumReason unifies standard and query-conditioned summarization with Direct Visual, Temporal Reasoning, High-Level Semantic Understanding, and External Knowledge Reasoning query categories. Multiple annotators score videos to analyze agreement and query-induced shifts toward salient or secondary events.
FH6pNJfJ8c.key_idea: Pair the same videos with reasoning queries and query-independent annotations to measure how requested intent changes the selected summary.
FH6pNJfJ8c.evidence: The benchmark contains 37 videos, 60 video-query pairs, 25 query-independent annotation sets, and 850 annotations from 10 annotators, with evaluation of >15 summarization methods.
FH6pNJfJ8c.claimed_gains: Query-conditioned summaries overlap with standard summaries by only 30–40% on average, indicating substantial query-induced shifts.
FH6pNJfJ8c.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the reasoning-query taxonomy and evidence that query-conditioned summarization differs materially from generic saliency selection.
FH6pNJfJ8c.main_concern: References derived from independent shot scores and knapsack selection may not measure summary-level redundancy, coverage, or continuity.

H96UH5u8yQ.one_liner: Decomposes MLLM hidden states into egocentric and altercentric subspaces, showing egocentric magnitude dominance drives perspective-taking failures.
H96UH5u8yQ.problem: Multimodal large language models exhibit strong egocentric bias in visuospatial perspective taking (VSPT), failing to adopt an altercentric viewpoint when perspectives conflict.
H96UH5u8yQ.method: Using controlled scenes that independently vary egocentric and altercentric spatial relations, the authors apply linear probes and decompose hidden representations into egocentric and altercentric components to measure their projections along the decision direction. Guided by the finding that egocentric components have systematically larger magnitude under conflict, they perform inference-time magnitude and alignment interventions.
H96UH5u8yQ.key_idea: Projects hidden states onto class-mean egocentric and altercentric subspaces to diagnose and intervene on the magnitude imbalance along the ego-alter decision direction.
H96UH5u8yQ.evidence: Linear probing, subspace decomposition, and representation interventions on controlled scenes with agent-disjoint folds and transfer evaluations on natural-image VSPT benchmarks.
H96UH5u8yQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled agent-disjoint experimental design that cleanly separates whether altercentric spatial information is encoded from whether the model uses it.
H96UH5u8yQ.main_concern: Reviewers note that down-scaling the egocentric component sharply degrades non-conflict accuracy (e.g., from 94.23% to 46.15% on Qwen), suggesting generic answer suppression rather than perspective restoration, compounded by hyperparameter selection on test performance.

M3COCwa5Fw.one_liner: Derives a minimax-optimal capped interaction-and-audit budget allocation with midpoint shrinkage for evaluating policy updates under censored rewards.
M3COCwa5Fw.problem: When reward feedback is censored, a policy update can appear to improve simply because its failures are observed less often, and auditing missing rewards is constrained by both limited audit budgets and scarce action arrivals.
M3COCwa5Fw.method: For finite action spaces and bounded rewards in [0,1], the authors characterize the worst-case estimation error under joint interaction and audit budgets and derive a single allocation rule capped by expected outcome availability paired with midpoint shrinkage. They extend the guarantees to adaptive sequential policy updates using interval screening, fresh-sample validation, and sequential early stopping.
M3COCwa5Fw.key_idea: Allocates interaction and missing-reward audit budgets proportionally up to an outcome-availability cap and applies midpoint shrinkage to balance sampling variance against partial-identification bias.
M3COCwa5Fw.evidence: Theoretical minimax bounds and empirical evaluations on controlled learning environments, fixed Qwen2.5-generated GSM8K responses, and historical TREC-COVID judgments.
M3COCwa5Fw.claimed_gains: With midpoint shrinkage, the capped allocation attains the minimax estimation error up to universal constants across confidence scales.
M3COCwa5Fw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-structured theoretical analysis of coupled interaction and audit budgets and the availability-capped allocation across confidence scales.
M3COCwa5Fw.main_concern: Reviewers note that the proposed optimal allocation and shrinkage yield negligible practical gains over uniform allocation in most experiments, and that artificial missingness on cheap-to-verify GSM8K outputs does not reflect genuinely costly auditing.

cB0hYIqF9I.one_liner: Models molecular conformer ensembles via permutation-equivariant symmetric and antisymmetric pair tensors along aligned covalent paths.
cB0hYIqF9I.problem: Modeling molecular conformer ensembles as generic unordered sets ignores the exact correspondence of atoms, bonds, angles, and torsions shared across conformers of the same molecular graph before ensemble aggregation.
cB0hYIqF9I.method: PaSTNet introduces the Pathwise State Tensor (PaST) operator, which lifts aligned conformer path states for each covalent path into channel-valued symmetric and antisymmetric pair tensors, contextualizes them via permutation-equivariant linear operations, and contracts them back into conformer updates. It incorporates a singleton-centered residual so each block reduces to the identity for a single conformer, alternating with geometry-conditioned graph propagation.
cB0hYIqF9I.key_idea: Lifts aligned covalent path states across conformers into symmetric and antisymmetric pairwise conformer tensors with singleton-centered residuals before pooling.
cB0hYIqF9I.evidence: Theoretical completeness characterization of the linear equivariant operator and empirical evaluations on molecular property prediction benchmarks (including ESOL, FreeSolv, and Lipo).
cB0hYIqF9I.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exploiting exact graph alignment across conformers via pathwise pairwise tensors before pooling is a clear, well-motivated architectural idea.
cB0hYIqF9I.main_concern: Reviewers note that empirical gains over strong baselines and even the single-conformer (K=1) variant are very small and well within cross-split standard deviations, questioning whether the cross-conformer tensor complexity drives performance.

tG6YQWpmwy.one_liner: Fine-tunes reasoning LLMs to self-predict intermediate answer confidence on 600 problems, shortening inference traces without length penalties or stopping rules.
tG6YQWpmwy.problem: Reasoning language models generate overly long reasoning traces, and existing efficiency methods require either inference-time early-stopping heuristics or explicit training length penalties that alter generation objectives.
tG6YQWpmwy.method: The authors propose a self-supervised procedure that fine-tunes reasoning models on 600 problems to predict their own probability-based answer confidence at intermediate points along their reasoning trajectories, with no length penalty or stopping objective. At inference time, the model uses standard autoregressive generation without eliciting confidence tokens or applying early-stopping rules.
tG6YQWpmwy.key_idea: Supervises intermediate self-predicted answer confidence along model-generated reasoning traces during fine-tuning while keeping inference-time decoding completely unmodified.
tG6YQWpmwy.evidence: Evaluated across Gemma, Qwen, Nemotron, and GPT-OSS model families on five mathematical, scientific, and coding reasoning benchmarks.
tG6YQWpmwy.claimed_gains: Self-supervised confidence fine-tuning reduces generated tokens by up to 25% while largely maintaining accuracy across Gemma, Qwen, Nemotron, and GPT-OSS models using only 600 training problems.
tG6YQWpmwy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical simplicity of requiring no gold labels, external judges, or inference-time stopping mechanisms while achieving consistent token reductions across model families.
tG6YQWpmwy.main_concern: Reviewers question whether accuracy is truly preserved given statistically significant drops on benchmarks like LiveCodeBench, note precedent in prior confidence-supervision work, and point out inconsistent baseline training and checkpoint selection protocols.

8OrJiIAySz.one_liner: Formulates controllable robotic manipulation across heterogeneous spatiotemporal constraints as diffusion action inpainting over a masked Cartesian action space.
8OrJiIAySz.problem: Controlling and editing generative robot policies through diverse spatiotemporal references such as keypoints, flows, orientations, and keyposes typically requires separate specialized interfaces.
8OrJiIAySz.method: The authors introduce the Masked Action Space (MAP) interface, treating heterogeneous spatiotemporal references as partial specifications of the same temporal Cartesian end-effector action trajectory. They train an Inpainting Policy (IP) with progress-guided alignment and multi-mask training to reconstruct missing action dimensions, paired with a training-free iterative RePaint denoising step.
8OrJiIAySz.key_idea: Represents keypoints, flows, orientations, and poses as partial masks in a unified temporal Cartesian action space and reconstructs unmasked dimensions via diffusion inpainting.
8OrJiIAySz.evidence: Evaluated on ManiSkill, LIBERO-10, and real-world robotic manipulation tasks.
8OrJiIAySz.claimed_gains: Achieves average task success rates of 92.67% on ManiSkill and 64.67% on LIBERO-10, and real-world spatiotemporal control with average positional and rotational errors of 44.3 mm and 7°.
8OrJiIAySz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the intuitive formulation unifying diverse spatial and temporal control references as partial masks in a single Cartesian action space for trajectory inpainting.
8OrJiIAySz.main_concern: Reviewers note that converting real-world task references into Cartesian action masks is non-trivial, baselines are weak or unconditioned on the references given to IP (with low 64.67% LIBERO-10 performance), and held-out compositional editing evaluation is narrow.

dkiCPDAmev.one_liner: Jailbreaks aligned LLMs in a multi-turn black-box setting by assigning negative in-context rewards to the target model's own prior refusals.
dkiCPDAmev.problem: Existing black-box LLM jailbreaks are expensive because many-shot attacks require curated harmful demonstrations while multi-turn attacks rely on capable external attacker LLMs.
dkiCPDAmev.method: SimJIR (Simple Jailbreaking with In-context Rewards) treats a target LLM's own refusal responses as free, on-policy negative demonstrations. Across multiple conversation turns, it assigns a negative scalar reward to each refusal, maintains a cumulative score, and prompts the target model to maximize its reward until it generates a harmful response.
dkiCPDAmev.key_idea: Repurposes the target model's own refusals as multi-turn negative demonstrations by appending negative in-context reward scores and instructing the model to maximize cumulative reward.
dkiCPDAmev.evidence: Evaluated across multiple open-source 4B–9B model families, two defense methods, and a multimodal TYPO subset.
dkiCPDAmev.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simplicity and low cost of the attack, which requires neither external attacker LLMs nor curated harmful demonstrations, as well as the reasoning-trace analysis.
dkiCPDAmev.main_concern: Reviewers note that all tested models are small open-source 4–9B models (omitting proprietary models like GPT-4o/Claude and recent baselines like TAP or ActorAttack), reasoning models can easily detect and reject the reward-maximization meta-prompt, and defense bypasses rely on manual prompt edits.

FsUeKY4edN.one_liner: Decomposes the VLM text-vision accuracy gap into relay-state formation and post-relay context execution, distilling coupled corrections via FCRD.
FsUeKY4edN.problem: Vision-language models often achieve lower accuracy on visual inputs than on semantically matched textual inputs even though both modalities are processed by the same language decoder.
FsUeKY4edN.method: Through causal state-interchange interventions across paired visual and textual tasks, the authors identify an intermediate cross-modal relay layer where decision states transfer bidirectionally, separating state Formation from post-relay context-conditioned Execution. They introduce Factorized Counterfactual Relay Distillation (FCRD), a lightweight corrector that jointly updates the relay state and surrounding context.
FsUeKY4edN.key_idea: Localizes an intermediate cross-modal relay state via causal interchange and trains a lightweight corrector to jointly distill textual state formation and post-relay context execution.
FsUeKY4edN.evidence: Evaluated across four vision-language models and five paired text-vision tasks.
FsUeKY4edN.claimed_gains: Across four VLMs and five paired tasks, FCRD closes over 60% of the text-vision performance gap on average.
FsUeKY4edN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the systematic causal interchange analysis that traces where the cross-modal performance gap arises and motivates the corrector architecture.
FsUeKY4edN.main_concern: Reviewers note that FCRD is trained with ground-truth labels but lacks comparisons against parameter-matched supervised baselines (such as LoRA or cross-entropy-only training at other layers), and evaluation is restricted to simple controlled tasks.

FrVMH1jHGc.one_liner: Compresses VLM Mixture-of-Experts without retraining by selecting experts via eigenbasis pivoting on a routing-aware Gram matrix and reconstructing routing weights.
FrVMH1jHGc.problem: Expert pools in vision-language Mixture-of-Experts (VLM-MoE) models are difficult to prune because visual tokens route across experts far more diffusely than text tokens, causing frequency-based pruning to collapse.
FrVMH1jHGc.method: The proposed method (SPARE) constructs a routing-aware expert-output Gram matrix on calibration data and pivots on its eigenbasis to select a well-conditioned subset of experts. From the same principal subspace basis, it reconstructs the discarded routing coordinates in closed form as a one-shot, retraining-free procedure.
FrVMH1jHGc.key_idea: Pivots on the eigenbasis of a routing-aware expert-output Gram matrix to select retained experts and remaps discarded routing weights in closed form.
FrVMH1jHGc.evidence: Evaluated on Kimi-VL-A3B and Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B across multiple expert retention budgets.
FrVMH1jHGc.claimed_gains: Covering 90% of visual routing events takes up to 1.8x as many experts as text; at 50% expert retention, frequency pruning keeps only 51–53% of dense performance, whereas the proposed method outperforms the strongest baseline by up to 3.6 points.
FrVMH1jHGc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the unified, retraining-free linear-algebraic formulation that couples expert subset selection with closed-form routing reconstruction and performs well under aggressive compression.
FrVMH1jHGc.main_concern: Reviewers point out a mismatch between the linear subspace reconstruction theory and the nonlinear top-k truncation/renormalization used at inference, alongside limited gains at moderate compression (75% retention) and missing SVD-MoE baselines.

ELRcwKxD3l.one_liner: Trains 4B/32B autoregressive and diffusion Lean theorem provers using difficulty-curriculum SFT, reasoning filtering, and self-distilled statement mutations.
ELRcwKxD3l.problem: LLM-based formal theorem provers demand high training and inference compute due to scarce formally verified proof data and overly long reasoning traces.
ELRcwKxD3l.method: Pythagoras-Prover trains 4B and 32B autoregressive Lean provers (plus a tactic-masked diffusion prover) using curriculum SFT stratified by proof difficulty and dynamic proof-reasoning filtering within an 8K-token budget. It expands training data via Augmented Lean Formalisation (ALF), which generates structured mutations of verified statements and populates proofs via self-distillation without formal verification of every variant.
ELRcwKxD3l.key_idea: Combines difficulty-stratified curriculum SFT and 8K-context reasoning filtering with self-distillation over synthetically mutated Lean theorem statements.
ELRcwKxD3l.evidence: Evaluated on MiniF2F-Test and PutnamBench using Pythagoras-Prover-4B, Pythagoras-Prover-32B, and a diffusion-based prover variant.
ELRcwKxD3l.claimed_gains: Pythagoras-Prover-4B achieves 86.1% pass@32 on MiniF2F-Test (surpassing DeepSeek-Prover-V2-671B at 82.4% with ~167x fewer parameters), while Pythagoras-Prover-32B reaches 93.0% on MiniF2F-Test and solves 93 of 672 PutnamBench problems.
ELRcwKxD3l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers are impressed by the strong MiniF2F and PutnamBench pass@32 performance at the 4B and 32B scales and value the exploratory diffusion prover experiment.
ELRcwKxD3l.main_concern: Reviewers note that ablations do not isolate ALF statement mutation from standard self-distillation or extra training tokens, compute-efficiency claims rely on an idealized proxy ignoring proof-search accuracy loss, and descriptions of the reasoning filter conflict between sections.

enLPR30GmE.one_liner: Co-trains a latent-action world model in one stage from sparsely labeled video by conditioning labeled forward predictions on posterior means.
enLPR30GmE.problem: Training robotic world models requires scarce action-labeled trajectories, and single-stage variational training on mixed labeled and unlabeled video causes the forward model to ignore sampled latent actions or collapse.
enLPR30GmE.method: JEVA jointly trains an inverse dynamics model, a latent forward model, and an action decoder in a single stage using continuous Gaussian latent actions grounded by a small fraction of action labels. To prevent the posterior-variance penalty from causing latent collapse, Variance-Reduced Routing (VRR) conditions the forward model on the posterior mean for labeled transitions while retaining posterior sampling on unlabeled transitions.
enLPR30GmE.key_idea: Co-trains inverse dynamics, latent forward dynamics, and action decoding in one stage while routing posterior means on labeled transitions and posterior samples on unlabeled transitions.
enLPR30GmE.evidence: Evaluated with CEM planning and behavioral cloning policies on robotic control tasks including PushT, Cube-Double, Cube-Triple, and Reacher under 5%–20% label fractions.
enLPR30GmE.claimed_gains: Without VRR, a warm-up stage collapses every latent dimension and single-stage training loses 14 percentage points (improving from 61.0% to 75.0% on PushT with 5% labels).
enLPR30GmE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, single-stage architecture and the concrete ablation showing VRR improves PushT performance by 14 points under sparse action labels.
enLPR30GmE.main_concern: Reviewers note that baselines are trained only on the 5%–20% labeled subset while JEVA sees all frames (omitting pseudo-labeling or unlabeled latent-action baselines like CLAM), and an ablation conditioning on posterior means for both labeled and unlabeled branches is missing.

dBSJp7CZkI.one_liner: Estimates per-client bias energies from trajectory disagreement in federated learning to compute minimax-optimal bias-cancelling aggregation weights.
dBSJp7CZkI.problem: Fixed aggregation weights in federated learning suffer from irreducible excess risk proportional to aggregate client bias energy that no optimizer can eliminate.
dBSJp7CZkI.method: Modeling clients as noisy views of a common truth with independent mean-zero distortions, the authors show that expected per-client bias second moments are identifiable from pairwise client disagreement via a well-conditioned linear inversion. They propose CROWD, which estimates these bias energies directly along the optimization trajectory without extra gradient queries and sets client aggregation weights inversely proportional to them.
dBSJp7CZkI.key_idea: Inverts the pairwise client gradient-disagreement matrix along the optimization trajectory to estimate per-client bias energies and reweights client updates inversely.
dBSJp7CZkI.evidence: Bayesian minimax lower and upper bound proofs, controlled synthetic experiments, and natural-client federated learning benchmarks including FEMNIST.
dBSJp7CZkI.claimed_gains: CROWD matches the Bayesian minimax lower bound up to the same constant without extra gradient queries.
dBSJp7CZkI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical distinction between persistent client bias and stochastic gradient noise, as well as recovering bias energies from client disagreement without extra gradient evaluations.
dBSJp7CZkI.main_concern: Reviewers find the theoretical assumptions (shared Hessian curvature, linear tilts, mean-zero independent incoherent biases, strong convexity) overly restrictive for realistic federated learning, noting that empirical gains vanish on larger natural client pools like 40-writer FEMNIST and CNNs.

G7Tr0y1pyj.one_liner: Controls false discovery rate in inductive top-k candidate selection via exact hypergeometric rank projection and Benjamini-Hochberg step-up thresholding.
G7Tr0y1pyj.problem: Standard conformal selection targets fixed outcome thresholds, whereas top-k membership depends jointly on the unobserved outcomes of the test pool and lives on a different rank scale than a differently sized calibration pool.
G7Tr0y1pyj.method: The authors propose crBH for inductive top-k selection with FDR control, using an exact rank projection to compute each calibration item's probability of falling outside the test top-k and combining these weights with trained ranking scores into projected conformal statistics. A null-proportion-adjusted Benjamini-Hochberg step-up rule selects the subset, alongside a conservative Certified-crBH variant for finite-sample exchangeability guarantees.
G7Tr0y1pyj.key_idea: Weights calibration items by their exact rank-projection probability of falling outside the test top-k to form conformal p-values for a null-adjusted Benjamini-Hochberg procedure.
G7Tr0y1pyj.evidence: Asymptotic FDR and power proofs, finite-sample exchangeability analysis for Certified-crBH, and empirical evaluations on controlled and application benchmarks.
G7Tr0y1pyj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending conformal FDR selection from fixed outcome cutoffs to relative test-pool top-k ranks via exact rank projection across pool sizes is novel and well-motivated.
G7Tr0y1pyj.main_concern: Reviewers note that the asymptotic theory assumes k/m converges to a positive constant (excluding sparse fixed-k regimes where Certified-crBH loses power), lacks comparisons to calibrated list-level selection methods like Learn-then-Test, and suffers from unclear notation in Section 4.

S9Vfr6Xaag.one_liner: Generates sparse counterfactual explanations for mixed-type tabular data using a mixed flow-matching operator and a feature-wise gating network.
S9Vfr6Xaag.problem: Existing counterfactual explanation methods for tabular data perturb numerical features slightly rather than leaving unselected numerical features exactly unchanged.
S9Vfr6Xaag.method: FlowCF formulates model-agnostic counterfactual generation as sparse distribution transport from the factual to the target class using flow matching extended with a mixed flow operator for continuous and categorical features. A feature-wise gating network zeroes out changes on unselected dimensions to enforce exact numerical sparsity during amortized inference.
S9Vfr6Xaag.key_idea: Pairs a mixed-type tabular flow-matching transport operator with a learned feature-wise gating network that masks unselected numerical velocity updates to zero.
S9Vfr6Xaag.evidence: Evaluated across six mixed-type tabular benchmark datasets against model-agnostic and gradient-based counterfactual baselines.
S9Vfr6Xaag.claimed_gains: Across six benchmark datasets, FlowCF changes 16% of numerical features on average compared to 22% for the next best method, with 30% lower numerical displacement.
S9Vfr6Xaag.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical, fast, model-agnostic amortized setup and the gating mechanism that achieves exact zero perturbation on unselected numerical features.
S9Vfr6Xaag.main_concern: Reviewers point out that exact zero-change sparsity favors FlowCF by construction over continuous baselines (requesting epsilon-threshold sparsity comparisons), that average proximity gains are confounded by zeroed features, and that distribution-level nearest-neighbor pairing may not capture instance-specific counterfactuals.

O8tdKaQ0Nj.one_liner: Measures memorization-to-generalization transitions in autoregressive transformers via maximal-coupling survival probability and predictive subspace overlap, analyzed on spiked Markov chains.
O8tdKaQ0Nj.problem: Diffusion model generalization tests based on coupling two independently trained models via shared latent noise cannot be directly applied to autoregressive transformers over discrete tokens.
O8tdKaQ0Nj.method: The authors define survival probability—the probability that two transformers trained on disjoint data subsets generate identical token sequences under maximal coupling—alongside an overlap measure of the leading principal components of next-token probability distributions.
