rwRyrGOG1L.one_liner: Recovers low-bit PTQ accuracy via two-stage pre- and post-reconstruction adaptation of normalization-affine parameters around the quantizer backend.
rwRyrGOG1L.problem: Low-bit post-training quantization severely degrades LLM accuracy, and it is unclear which low-dimensional parameter subspace best recovers task performance under tight budgets.
rwRyrGOG1L.method: NormSub adapts only normalization-affine parameters in two stages: a pre-stage trains affine parameters on a disposable quantized proxy and transfers them back to floating-point weights before fresh PTQ reconstruction, and a post-stage refines exposed affine parameters while freezing non-affine weights.
rwRyrGOG1L.key_idea: Adapts normalization-affine parameters in a pre-PTQ disposable-proxy stage and a post-PTQ refinement stage to recover low-bit quantized accuracy.
rwRyrGOG1L.evidence: Evaluated on dense LLMs (including Qwen3-8B and Llama3-8B at W2A4KV4 and W3A16) across multiple PTQ backends (AWQ, GPTQ, GPTAQ, QuaRot+ResComp) and ImageNet.
rwRyrGOG1L.claimed_gains: On Qwen3-8B W2A4KV4 with QuaRot+ResComp, six-task mean accuracy increases from 49.62% to 58.05% (49.6% to 58.1% rounded).
rwRyrGOG1L.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree normalization-affine adaptation is simple, backend-agnostic, adds zero inference overhead, and recovers substantial accuracy at extreme low bit widths.
rwRyrGOG1L.main_concern: Reviewers find post-stage adaptation alone captures almost all gains while the pre-stage doubles PTQ passes without wall-clock comparisons, and note missing comparisons to Norm Tweaking.

sR0dbwZcZU.one_liner: Trains a multi-granularity agent judge via SFT-DPO-GRPO and co-evolves it bidirectionally with the agent policy.
sR0dbwZcZU.problem: Static outcome-only LLM judges miss local action quality and evolving execution-state errors in multi-step agent trajectories.
sR0dbwZcZU.method: AgentJudge derives step, dynamic-prefix, and outcome supervision from search and coding trajectories, trains progressively with SFT, future-masked retrospective DPO, and GRPO, and co-evolves with the agent via bidirectional updates.
sR0dbwZcZU.key_idea: Train a judge on local step, dynamic prefix, and outcome supervision using future-masked retrospective preference pairs, then co-evolve agent and judge bidirectionally.
sR0dbwZcZU.evidence: Experiments evaluate general response judging, agent trajectory judging (e.g., Plan-RewardBench, AgentRewardBench), and a small co-evolution study.
sR0dbwZcZU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating local steps, prefixes, and outcomes jointly from real trajectories addresses an important gap in agent evaluation.
sR0dbwZcZU.main_concern: Reviewers note insufficient detail on how judge feedback trains the agent, small DPO data size (311 pairs), and ablations that do not isolate individual supervision granularities.

ij0zRWqZHl.one_liner: Identifies the confidence shortcut in masked diffusion models where confidence-ordered decoding violates logical reasoning dependencies.
ij0zRWqZHl.problem: Masked diffusion models using confidence-based decoding can commit early to plausible tokens while skipping intermediate logical dependencies.
ij0zRWqZHl.method: The authors diagnose this confidence shortcut by comparing confidence-ordered decoding against dependency-aligned oracle orders and testing confidence-aligned training schemes across reasoning tasks.
ij0zRWqZHl.key_idea: Compare fixed-model decoding orders and confidence-aligned training objectives on dependency-structured reasoning tasks to expose premature high-confidence token commitments.
ij0zRWqZHl.evidence: Controlled pretraining experiments on multi-digit addition, Maze, ListOps, Countdown, and Sudoku, plus LLaDA-8B Base evaluations, support the analysis.
ij0zRWqZHl.claimed_gains: Confidence-aligned training schemes can increase addition error rates by an order of magnitude.
ij0zRWqZHl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean diagnostic setup separating decoding order from model capability and the precise error analysis of premature commitments.
ij0zRWqZHl.main_concern: Reviewers note that order-selection gaps appear consistently only on Addition and Maze tail strata rather than across all tasks, and question unvalidated reimplementations of baselines like PAPL.

QCNxXWObrg.one_liner: Overlaps successive VLA model inferences across mobile GPU and NPU via an offline-profiled periodic pipeline schedule.
QCNxXWObrg.problem: Mobile SoCs struggle to run vision-language-action (VLA) models fast enough for high-frequency robot control.
QCNxXWObrg.method: VLA-Duo profiles GPU-NPU operator timings with inter-accelerator interference offline and replays a single-cut periodic pipeline schedule that overlaps successive VLA inferences at runtime.
QCNxXWObrg.key_idea: Partition VLA execution across mobile GPU and NPU using an interference-aware offline periodic schedule to overlap consecutive inferences.
QCNxXWObrg.evidence: Hardware benchmarks run pi_0 and pi_0.5 on Snapdragon 8 Elite and 8 Elite Gen 5 SoCs, alongside separate LIBERO simulations under a 10-step delay.
QCNxXWObrg.claimed_gains: VLA-Duo achieves 36.1-78.3% higher throughput than ExecuTorch/QNN NPU with 394-499 ms output periods (10.0-12.7 Hz equivalent control), and pi_0.5 reaches 92.8% average success in LIBERO simulations under a ten-control-step delay.
QCNxXWObrg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the heterogeneous GPU-NPU pipelining addresses a concrete mobile deployment bottleneck and improves short-run throughput.
QCNxXWObrg.main_concern: Reviewers point out that hardware timings and LIBERO control evaluations are decoupled, thermal throttling/power are untested in short 20-inference runs, and no real robot is evaluated.

LGfuFWWvxO.one_liner: Trains a graph attention policy with GRPO to select and order evaluation rubrics for frozen LLM judges.
LGfuFWWvxO.problem: Rubric selection and ordering strongly affect LLM-as-a-Judge agreement with human ratings even when rubric content is fixed.
LGfuFWWvxO.method: GraphRubric encodes rubrics as nodes in a graph attention network conditioned on the input case and uses GRPO-style sampling to assign advantages to directed execution-order edges without modifying judge weights.
LGfuFWWvxO.key_idea: Uses a graph attention controller trained with GRPO edge-level advantages to select and order rubric prompts for a frozen LLM judge.
LGfuFWWvxO.evidence: Experiments on SummEval, HANNA, and USR datasets using DeepSeek, GLM, and Gemini judges.
LGfuFWWvxO.claimed_gains: On SummEval, HANNA, and USR, three DeepSeek seeds reduce the primary error metric by 13.6%, 20.5%, and 5.8%, respectively, relative to uniform path sampling.
LGfuFWWvxO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate optimizing rubric presentation for closed-API judges without weight updates and the thorough reproducibility documentation.
LGfuFWWvxO.main_concern: Diagnostics show the controller often collapses to a single global path across test cases rather than case-conditioned routing, and standard prompt-optimization baselines are missing.

X9lHKZyoNr.one_liner: Pretrains MILP graph representations with contrastive invariance to re-descriptions and hypernetwork-predicted equivariance to variable substitutions.
X9lHKZyoNr.problem: Learning general-purpose representations for mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs) without solver-derived labels requires exploiting equivalent formulations without conflating invariant and variable-transforming changes.
X9lHKZyoNr.method: ReMILP characterizes all instance-independent affine MILP reformulations into variable-preserving re-descriptions and unimodular substitutions. It jointly trains a graph neural network and a hypernetwork via equivariant contrastive learning to enforce invariance to re-descriptions and predictable embedding transformations under substitutions.
X9lHKZyoNr.key_idea: Jointly trains a GNN and hypernetwork with self-supervised contrastive objectives enforcing invariance to MILP re-descriptions and equivariance to affine variable substitutions.
X9lHKZyoNr.evidence: Supported by completeness theorems for affine MILP reformulations and experiments on binary solution, constraint activity, and integrality gap prediction, plus runtime tests against default Gurobi.
X9lHKZyoNr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical characterization of valid affine MILP reformulations and the clean mapping from re-descriptions and substitutions to invariance and equivariance objectives.
X9lHKZyoNr.main_concern: Reviewers point out the lack of end-to-end solver-level evaluations (such as branching or wall-clock solving benchmarks) and incomplete baseline comparisons against generic GNN contrastive learning.

4tcIEkRcdM.one_liner: Trains hierarchical LLM agents with bidirectional cross-level on-policy self-distillation between global plans and local execution decisions.
4tcIEkRcdM.problem: Existing hierarchical planning methods rely on learned value models or process rewards that fail to connect terminal execution evidence to global plans and task-wide context to local subgoals.
4tcIEkRcdM.method: HiCLA supplements GRPO with training-only cross-level self-distillation after trajectory termination. The policy generates terminal evidence to rescore the global plan and produces a revised plan to rescore recorded local states and decisions under original generation contexts.
4tcIEkRcdM.key_idea: Uses post-trajectory terminal evidence to rescore global plans and hindsight revised plans to rescore local execution likelihoods as auxiliary GRPO training signals.
4tcIEkRcdM.evidence: Evaluated across three Qwen backbones (including 4B and 7B) on τ²-bench over four seeds and held-out BFCL-V3, along with component ablations.
4tcIEkRcdM.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest τ²-bench mean success among compared methods and exceeds the strongest baseline on held-out BFCL-V3 with 7B and 4B models by up to 5.25%.
4tcIEkRcdM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the bidirectional cross-level credit assignment design that keeps deployed policies free of hindsight information during inference.
4tcIEkRcdM.main_concern: Reviewers note that likelihood changes under hindsight revised plans are not independently validated as causal or accurate measures of local decision quality.

GcZQrpVMWp.one_liner: Enables multi-user homomorphic transformer inference via Boolean-domain dense/sparse collective key setup and interleaved ciphertext packing.
GcZQrpVMWp.problem: Existing homomorphic encryption transformer inference assumes a single key owner and cannot support distributed setup for sparse-secret encapsulation across independent users.
GcZQrpVMWp.method: The framework uses a reusable two-server-assisted setup that samples dense and fixed-weight sparse collective secrets in the Boolean-sharing domain and defers RNS conversion until key generation. Multi-user ciphertexts are consolidated via interleaved packing for shared Transformer evaluation, followed by per-user extraction and synchronized threshold decryption.
GcZQrpVMWp.key_idea: Samples dense and sparse-secret encapsulation keys in Boolean secret sharing before RNS conversion, then packs multi-user ciphertexts for shared Transformer evaluation.
GcZQrpVMWp.evidence: Benchmarked with 16 users comparing shared encrypted inference service time, interface overhead, and task accuracy against plaintext and single-user encrypted inference.
GcZQrpVMWp.claimed_gains: With 16 users, shared inference reduces service time by 15.998x with 0.00064% interface overhead while maintaining accuracy within 0.3 percentage points of plaintext inference.
GcZQrpVMWp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-user threshold-CKKS problem is well-motivated and the Boolean-first distributed key setup protocol is technically thoughtful.
GcZQrpVMWp.main_concern: Reviewers note missing end-to-end SSE-enabled vs. non-SSE full-inference ablations, uninstantiated security parameters, and strict user participation requirements for decryption.

Qn7QNDbK1o.one_liner: Pretrains a 6.3M-parameter masked autoencoder with a physical-depth-aligned tokenizer on 24.8M wearable A-mode ultrasound scans.
Qn7QNDbK1o.problem: Wearable A-mode ultrasound models are trained from scratch per subject, task, and hardware platform because no compact cross-device foundation model exists.
Qn7QNDbK1o.method: FOCUS is a 6.3M-parameter masked autoencoder pretrained on 24.8 million unlabeled A-mode ultrasound scans spanning five acquisition systems and multiple body sites. It uses a frequency-aware tokenizer that aligns patches to physical tissue depth to handle heterogeneous sampling rates across devices.
Qn7QNDbK1o.key_idea: Pretrains a compact 6.3M masked autoencoder on 24.8M heterogeneous A-mode ultrasound scans using a sampling-frequency-aware tokenizer aligned to physical tissue depth.
Qn7QNDbK1o.evidence: Evaluated on eight subject-specific classification and kinematic regression tasks across five wearable datasets, including an unseen acquisition platform (UltraPro).
Qn7QNDbK1o.claimed_gains: Fine-tuning FOCUS with 40% of labeled data outperforms training the same architecture from scratch with 100% of labels on all eight tasks.
Qn7QNDbK1o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the large-scale pretraining corpus and physically motivated depth-aligned tokenizer yield consistent label-efficiency gains across diverse AUS tasks.
Qn7QNDbK1o.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the frequency-aware tokenizer is not ablated against fixed-patch or resampled baselines and question zero-shot generalization claims.

NQnDcaPkdQ.one_liner: Integrates a scratch-trained audio encoder, DeepStack cross-layer injection, and explicit time markers for unified audio-language understanding.
NQnDcaPkdQ.problem: Unified audio understanding requires combining semantic content with fine-grained acoustic cues and temporal alignment across speech, environmental sounds, and music.
NQnDcaPkdQ.method: MOSS-Audio trains an audio encoder from scratch, injects multi-level features into the language decoder via DeepStack, and anchors features with explicit time markers. An event-boundary segmentation and specialist-merging pipeline builds training data for staged Instruct and Thinking post-training.
NQnDcaPkdQ.key_idea: Combines a scratch-trained audio encoder, cross-layer DeepStack feature injection, explicit time markers, and event-segmented caption data in Instruct and Thinking variants.
NQnDcaPkdQ.evidence: Evaluated across public audio understanding, speech-captioning, and timestamp alignment benchmarks against open-source (up to 30B) and proprietary omni-models.
NQnDcaPkdQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge strong empirical breadth and competitive unified audio performance with a compact 8B backbone.
NQnDcaPkdQ.main_concern: Reviewers criticize insufficient ablations isolating DeepStack, event-guided segmentation, and explicit time markers at the 4B/8B model scales.

GB69WeYSgJ.one_liner: Aggregates distant tokens into multi-level memory tokens via a timestamped causal mask for logarithmic KV-cache growth.
GB69WeYSgJ.problem: Autoregressive Transformer KV caches grow linearly with sequence length, creating severe memory and throughput bottlenecks on long contexts.
GB69WeYSgJ.method: MANTA maintains fixed-size windows at hierarchical aggregation levels, progressively compressing distant tokens into learned memory tokens via a unified timestamp-based causal attention mask while keeping recent tokens at full resolution.
GB69WeYSgJ.key_idea: Uses a timestamp-based causal mask to recursively aggregate distant context into multi-level memory tokens, bounding KV-cache growth logarithmically.
GB69WeYSgJ.evidence: Adapts Llama 3.2 1B trained on 200B tokens and compares against dense and sliding-window attention on language modeling and RULER at 8K context.
GB69WeYSgJ.claimed_gains: Reduces KV-cache size by 97.8% at a context length of 8K tokens in a typical configuration.
GB69WeYSgJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the coherent hierarchical attention-mask formulation and substantial KV-cache memory savings.
GB69WeYSgJ.main_concern: Reviewers highlight poor long-context retrieval scores on RULER (0.176-0.180 vs. 0.585 dense) and missing comparisons with memory-matched windows or learned-compression baselines.

2JQs8j5Qsa.one_liner: Applies double machine learning to separate intentional system manipulation from baseline model errors and biases in content moderation.
2JQs8j5Qsa.problem: Auditors cannot easily distinguish intentional manipulation of ML systems from mundane model inaccuracy, unfairness, or bias.
2JQs8j5Qsa.method: The paper frames AI assurance as falsifiable hypothesis testing using Double Machine Learning (DML) to partial out a system's normal behavior as confounding variation and estimate manipulation treatment effects in content moderation.
2JQs8j5Qsa.key_idea: Uses double machine learning to partial out normal classifier error and bias patterns so intentional manipulation effects can be isolated.
2JQs8j5Qsa.evidence: Evaluated on the Jigsaw content moderation dataset under loss function manipulation, intentional bias amplification, and direct moderation-decision manipulation.
2JQs8j5Qsa.claimed_gains: On manipulation detection, DML achieves an AUC of 0.92 compared to fairness and statistical baselines around 0.76.
2JQs8j5Qsa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and tackles an important AI assurance problem with thorough experiments on content moderation manipulation.
2JQs8j5Qsa.main_concern: The evaluation is narrow—restricted to content moderation on Jigsaw with few causal or auditing baselines—and DML may struggle to separate intentional manipulation from unintended bias or confounders omitted by the auditor.

QXg5mWzuHK.one_liner: Calibrates conformal risk control at the patient level rather than window level for binary, multiclass, and tail-risk medical time series.
QXg5mWzuHK.problem: Applying conformal risk control to correlated time-series windows creates a sample-size illusion that fails to control risk for newly sampled patients.
QXg5mWzuHK.method: The authors formulate subject-aware conformal risk control calibrated directly over patients for binary false-negative-rate control and multiclass coverage, and extend it to subject-level conditional value-at-risk (CVaR) to control tail risk across patients.
QXg5mWzuHK.key_idea: Calibrates conformal risk control and CVaR tail-risk bounds over patient-level units rather than correlated sub-windows.
QXg5mWzuHK.evidence: Evaluated across 12 model architectures and three EEG/ECG medical time-series datasets.
QXg5mWzuHK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a practically relevant patient-versus-window calibration mismatch in medical time-series risk control.
QXg5mWzuHK.main_concern: The work is viewed as a straightforward adaptation of existing conformal risk control methods with unclear presentation, undefined notation, and limited subject counts in the three datasets.

salEzRHr4F.one_liner: Minimizing a quadratic Ising proxy jointly selects interacting Transformer blocks for removal under a fixed compression budget.
salEzRHr4F.problem: Independent block-ranking methods miss interactions among Transformer block-removal decisions when compressing large language models.
salEzRHr4F.method: The paper formulates block removal as constrained binary optimization mapped to an Ising glass. It selects low-energy block combinations, including nonconsecutive subsets, using energy as a proxy for downstream performance.
salEzRHr4F.key_idea: Off-diagonal terms in a quadratic binary objective model interactions between block removals and turn joint subset selection into energy minimization.
salEzRHr4F.evidence: Experiments cover 20 model-benchmark configurations, low-energy and high-energy removal states, MMLU, HellaSwag, and multiple Llama models and compression rates.
salEzRHr4F.claimed_gains: The method outperforms other methods in 13 out of 20 model-benchmark configurations, with MMLU gains of 21.5 and 22.9 percentage points at 37.5% and 50% compression for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct, respectively.
salEzRHr4F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that joint block selection and explicit interaction terms are valuable, especially at high compression rates.
salEzRHr4F.main_concern: Two reviewers focus on the dropped first-order Taylor term, arguing that the quadratic proxy's reliability needs stronger justification and validation.

jVsespZtnT.one_liner: Attributing and pruning GNN computation trees with Shapley values extracts prediction-specific circuits tied to input-graph elements.
jVsespZtnT.problem: Circuit discovery for mechanistic interpretability has focused on Transformers, leaving message-passing computations in graph neural networks largely unexamined.
jVsespZtnT.method: CircuitFACT constructs computation trees that represent message-passing dependencies, assigns Shapley-based attributions to their components, and trims the trees into compact circuits. The resulting circuits map back to input-graph elements.
jVsespZtnT.key_idea: Shapley attribution over explicit computation trees identifies and prunes the message-passing components supporting an individual GNN prediction.
jVsespZtnT.evidence: Reviews describe experiments on four small-scale binary classification datasets with three GNN architectures, including circuit visualizations and comparisons involving zero ablation.
jVsespZtnT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that applying Shapley-based circuit discovery to message-passing GNNs is principled and model-agnostic.
jVsespZtnT.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite the limited evaluation and absence of comparisons against standard post-hoc explanation methods.

M0XdmpjqN3.one_liner: Extends RoPE across token and lane dimensions with an inter-sequence attention mask so parallel LLM rollouts collaborate during generation.
M0XdmpjqN3.problem: Parallel test-time scaling methods like best-of-N generate candidate sequences independently without reusing intermediate reasoning across trajectories.
M0XdmpjqN3.method: LaneRoPE enables cross-sequence collaboration among N parallel generations using an inter-sequence attention mask and a RoPE extension encoding relative positions both within and across sequence lanes. The packed-lane layout reuses standard causal attention kernels with minimal architectural changes and low inference overhead.
M0XdmpjqN3.key_idea: Pairs an inter-sequence attention mask with a two-dimensional token-and-lane RoPE extension so parallel rollouts attend to each other's intermediate tokens.
M0XdmpjqN3.evidence: Evaluated on mathematical reasoning benchmarks using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B and 7B models across multiple lane counts with device-level latency measurements.
M0XdmpjqN3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the positional encoding design simple, practical to integrate into pretrained Transformers, and low-overhead at inference.
M0XdmpjqN3.main_concern: Reviewers note modest and inconsistent collaboration gains (+1.1pp maj@4 on 7B but -1.1pp on 1.5B KTO), lack of isolation from training data/KTO, narrow math-only evaluation, and a suspected sign error in the KTO equation.

ZkBCD3Iati.one_liner: Extracts parameter-free path signatures via Chen's identity and phase-plane scaling for battery degradation estimation within 1 MB edge SRAM.
ZkBCD3Iati.problem: Battery sequence models fail or exceed microcontroller memory bounds under real-world micro-fractured telemetry with short unanchored charging slices, quantization, and dropouts.
ZkBCD3Iati.method: RIIS-MicroBurst maps variable-length charging slices into fixed-dimensional geometric features using a parameter-free free Lie algebra path-signature operator computed incrementally via Chen's identity. It combines these signatures with thermodynamic phase-plane scaling, a closed-form Geometry-Oracle, and lightweight Ridge or MLP readouts.
ZkBCD3Iati.key_idea: Uses incremental Chen's-identity path signatures with thermodynamic phase-plane scaling to encode irregular variable-length battery slices into fixed-size features for lightweight edge readouts.
ZkBCD3Iati.evidence: Evaluated across simulation, dynamic stress, synthetic fault, and commercial fleet battery benchmarks with MAC counts and workstation latency profiling.
ZkBCD3Iati.claimed_gains: A 12-frame inference costs 55,365 multiply-accumulates with a Ridge readout and 76,913 with an MLP readout.
ZkBCD3Iati.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical focus on irregular edge battery telemetry and the mathematically grounded, memory-efficient fixed-dimensional path features.
ZkBCD3Iati.main_concern: Reviewers point out that cropping, quantization, and packet dropouts alter path geometry (so reparameterization invariance does not guarantee immunity), and that FLOP audits omit signature extraction costs and real MCU profiling.

ISODBMoFZI.one_liner: Attaches block-localized fast-weight neural memory plugins to frozen Transformers to compress long contexts at test time without backbone backpropagation.
ISODBMoFZI.problem: In-context learning becomes memory- and compute-intensive and degrades in accuracy as context lengths scale to 128K tokens.
ISODBMoFZI.method: MoNe attaches lightweight fast-weight memory modules to frozen pretrained Transformer layers and meta-trains them offline. At test time, it processes long contexts in segments via block-localized gradient updates without backpropagating through the backbone, then injects context-dependent residuals during query inference without feeding the original context.
ISODBMoFZI.key_idea: Writes segmented long contexts into layer-wise fast-weight memory plugins via block-localized test-time gradient updates without backbone backpropagation, injecting memory residuals during query inference.
ISODBMoFZI.evidence: Evaluated on RULER, BABILong, SQuAD, and HotpotQA up to 128K-token contexts (extrapolating from <=4K meta-training) with memory and FLOP accounting.
ISODBMoFZI.claimed_gains: Generalizes to 128K-token contexts while reducing both peak GPU memory and total FLOPs by approximately 80% relative to in-context learning at 128K.
ISODBMoFZI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the modular frozen-backbone design avoiding backbone-wide backpropagation, strong 4K-to-128K extrapolation, and cost accounting that includes memory writing.
ISODBMoFZI.main_concern: Reviewers note that task-specific meta-training confounds comparisons against unadapted ICL baselines, multi-query reuse is not directly evaluated, and scaling inner learning rate by total segment count conflicts with incremental extensibility.

9GxSwVur3u.one_liner: Discovers interpretable features from unstructured data by prompting LLMs for pairwise rationales and fitting a position-debiased statistical choice model.
9GxSwVur3u.problem: Opaque embeddings hinder interpretable decision-making on unstructured data, while prompting an LLM over whole datasets suffers from context limits and diluted attention.
9GxSwVur3u.method: The method asks an LLM to explain distinguishing features across pairwise item comparisons and groups these rationales into candidate features. It then fits a statistical choice model to the rationales to produce per-item, per-feature scores with confidence intervals, correct judge position bias, and filter unreliable features.
9GxSwVur3u.key_idea: Treats LLM pairwise comparison rationales as observations in a statistical choice model to estimate position-debiased per-item feature scores with uncertainty and reliability filtering.
9GxSwVur3u.evidence: Evaluated on a synthetic cover-letter hiring dataset with known ground-truth features, a Reddit CMV dataset, and unlabeled multi-agent LLM execution traces.
9GxSwVur3u.claimed_gains: Finds counterparts to 12 of 16 expert-identified failure categories on unlabeled multi-agent LLM execution traces.
9GxSwVur3u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem compelling and praise treating LLM pairwise rationales as data within a statistically rigorous, position-debiased choice model.
9GxSwVur3u.main_concern: Reviewers cite missing related-work comparisons (e.g., D5, VisDiff, LLooM, HypotheSAEs), small case-study scale, and modest real-data accuracy gains over zero-shot feature proposals (62.63% vs 61.25%).

eJunP19pmJ.one_liner: Adapts multi-turn agent on-policy self-distillation via divergence-progress step weighting and discrepancy-adaptive token support sizing.
eJunP19pmJ.problem: In multi-turn agentic on-policy self-distillation, uniform step weighting and fixed token-support budgets fail under accumulating state drift and varying teacher-student discrepancy.
eJunP19pmJ.method: HiSD combines progress-aware step supervision, which allocates step-level distillation weight according to relative divergence progress, with support-adaptive token supervision, which adjusts the token support size based on instantaneous teacher-student discrepancy to mitigate gradient conflicts with GRPO.
eJunP19pmJ.key_idea: Allocates step-level self-distillation weights by relative divergence progress and dynamically sizes token-level support sets according to teacher-student discrepancy.
eJunP19pmJ.evidence: Evaluated on ALFWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop across three Qwen2.5-Instruct model sizes against GRPO and recent OPSD baselines with component ablations.
eJunP19pmJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the targeted diagnosis of step- and token-level non-uniformity in multi-turn OPSD and the broad multi-benchmark, multi-scale empirical evaluation.
eJunP19pmJ.main_concern: Reviewers note discrepancies between the paper's method definition and public code (singleton support and trajectory averaging), heuristic KL-based rules lacking theoretical justification, and incremental novelty.

CSoTCflQb2.one_liner: Derives finite-sample upper confidence bounds on harmful actions from zero detections under strategic monitoring evasion and proposes equalized-coverage designs.
CSoTCflQb2.problem: Treating zero or few monitor detections as evidence of rare harm fails when a monitored AI system can infer where oversight is weak and concentrate harmful actions there.
CSoTCflQb2.method: Under invisible per-unit randomization and audited recall lower bounds, the authors derive model-free finite-sample upper confidence bounds on harmful actions parameterized by a concentration sensitivity factor Gamma. They show that average coverage and AUC fail to control the lower tail of posterior detection probability and propose equalizing effective coverage across strata.
CSoTCflQb2.key_idea: Combines invisible per-unit randomization with a Gamma-sensitivity bound on strategic harm concentration to certify finite-sample harm limits and motivate equalized-coverage monitoring.
CSoTCflQb2.evidence: Supported by theoretical finite-sample bounds, stratified monitoring design calculations, and partial-observation monitoring experiments.
CSoTCflQb2.claimed_gains: In a stratified design, a 95% bound of about 3 harmful actions under proportional allocation rises to 244 when harms are twice over-represented in weakly monitored traffic, whereas equalizing effective coverage yields a Gamma-robust bound of about 8.
CSoTCflQb2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exposing why zero detections and standard summary metrics fail under strategic evasion addresses a critical AI safety monitoring gap.
CSoTCflQb2.main_concern: Reviewers challenge the assumption of independent monitor success across units (since correlated attack blind spots break geometric decay), note difficult notation, and flag a footnote caveat on the Gamma=1 bound.

hYwAL5M9wZ.one_liner: Couples initial Gaussian noises across a diffusion batch while preserving standard-Gaussian marginals to control gallery diversity without overhead.
hYwAL5M9wZ.problem: Independent initial Gaussian noises in diffusion sampling limit control over batch-level diversity unless extra test-time optimization or modified guidance is added.
hYwAL5M9wZ.method: The paper designs analytic repulsive and learned joint couplings over initial noise batches that keep each individual noise vector marginally standard Gaussian, preserving single-sample quality. It provides marginal-invariance and optimality analyses and applies the coupling to image and video diffusion models alone or alongside existing diversity methods.
hYwAL5M9wZ.key_idea: Apply a marginal-preserving joint coupling transform to a batch of initial standard-Gaussian noises to induce cross-sample repulsion with negligible overhead.
hYwAL5M9wZ.evidence: Supported by marginal-invariance/optimality theory and experiments across image and video diffusion models, including combinations with CNO, PG, and CADS.
hYwAL5M9wZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that marginal-preserving initial-noise coupling is simple, virtually compute-free, preserves single-sample quality, and complements existing diversity methods.
hYwAL5M9wZ.main_concern: Core repulsive-coupling Algorithm 1 heavily overlaps with prior work (Jia et al., 2026a), semantic diversity gains over low-level pixel variation are weak, and improvements shrink at larger batch sizes (K=32).

upe1ENUjIT.one_liner: Uses parser error positions to mask local spans and regenerate them via diffusion language model infilling for structured outputs.
upe1ENUjIT.problem: Diffusion language models suffer low syntactic parsing rates on structured outputs, especially under small denoising-step budgets.
upe1ENUjIT.method: Parser-Guided Self-Repair (PGSR) runs an external parser on generated structured text, anchors on the reported error position, remasks a small surrounding token window, and reconstructs it using the DLM's native infilling. It requires no training and works across output formats.
upe1ENUjIT.key_idea: Anchor on a parser-reported syntax error location, mask a fixed local span around it, and infill the span in place using the diffusion language model.
upe1ENUjIT.evidence: Evaluated with LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B across tool calling, code generation, text-to-SQL, and molecular generation under varying denoising budgets.
upe1ENUjIT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that PGSR is simple, training-free, low-latency, and transfers well across structured domains, especially at low denoising budgets.
upe1ENUjIT.main_concern: Reviewers note moderate novelty, missing ablations and compute-matched retry baselines, and failure modes when fixed-window in-place replacement cannot handle insertions, deletions, or long-range syntax errors.

61aavh2kV9.one_liner: Varies training caption coverage while holding images fixed to show multi-object diffusion composition requires captions naming multiple objects together.
61aavh2kV9.problem: Prior explanations of compositional failures in text-to-image diffusion focus on denoiser locality or image coverage, overlooking that human captions leave most depicted objects unnamed.
61aavh2kV9.method: The authors define caption coverage as the fraction of multi-object training images whose captions name at least two objects, and vary it while fixing training images and architecture. They test whether summing single-object predictions restores composition in low-coverage models.
61aavh2kV9.key_idea: Hold multi-object training images fixed while systematically varying the fraction of captions naming multiple objects, and test single-object score summation to isolate caption-reading failures.
61aavh2kV9.evidence: Evaluated on controlled synthetic datasets (ShapeWorld, CLEVR) and real images (MS-COCO with Stable Diffusion v1.5 noted in reviews).
61aavh2kV9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating caption coverage from image coverage in controlled from-scratch experiments provides a clear, testable perspective on compositional generation.
61aavh2kV9.main_concern: Low-coverage models are tested on out-of-distribution multi-object prompt formats, and real-world validation is limited to object presence on Stable Diffusion v1.5 rather than modern models or binding/spatial tasks.

2aRM6OCjLl.one_liner: Applies Willems' fundamental lemma to define prompt informativity thresholds separating latent-system identification from model-free interpolation in in-context learning.
2aRM6OCjLl.problem: In-context learning succeeds on some prompts and fails on seemingly similar ones without a quantitative measure of whether the prompt contains enough excitation to determine the continuation.
2aRM6OCjLl.method: Viewing prompts as recorded input-output data, the paper uses Willems' fundamental lemma to establish excitation thresholds separating horizon-free latent-system identification from horizon-dependent model-free interpolation. It compares task-trained Transformers and pretrained open-weight LLMs against Bayes-optimal and data-enabled predictors.
2aRM6OCjLl.key_idea: Quantify prompt excitation via Willems' fundamental lemma to separate latent-system identification thresholds from higher-excitation model-free interpolation regimes in in-context learning.
2aRM6OCjLl.evidence: Supported by theoretical thresholds and probes on task-trained Transformers and pretrained open-weight LLMs (2.7B-120B across five families).
2aRM6OCjLl.claimed_gains: Task-trained Transformers reach their error floor two to three tones past the identification threshold and beat the data-enabled predictor several-fold throughout the gap.
2aRM6OCjLl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that framing prompt informativity through excitation richness is a compelling and well-motivated angle on when in-context learning works.
2aRM6OCjLl.main_concern: Reviewers flag incomplete theoretical proofs for discrete sequences (unverified rank/positivity assumptions in Theorem 3), hard-to-parse or underspecified empirics, and informal or overclaimed writing.

wkWQUXVuLZ.one_liner: Replaces CDLM self-conditioning with a two-level interpolant (DoubleCat) and discrete token reveals (SemiCat) to fix train-inference mismatch and identifiability.
wkWQUXVuLZ.problem: Training continuous diffusion language models relies on expensive self-conditioning and suffers from token-identifiability failures under high-norm Gaussian noise, with unclear underlying mechanisms.
wkWQUXVuLZ.method: The authors analyze self-conditioning and embedding geometry in CDLMs, proposing DoubleCat, a two-level interpolant that exposes the model to inference-like states without an extra training forward pass. Adding discrete token reveals yields SemiCat to directly resolve Gaussian token identifiability.
wkWQUXVuLZ.key_idea: Use a two-level categorical interpolant (DoubleCat) plus discrete token reveals (SemiCat) to mimic inference states and preserve token identifiability without extra self-conditioning forward passes.
wkWQUXVuLZ.evidence: Evaluated on TinyGSM and six likelihood-based benchmarks up to the 1.7B parameter scale, alongside noise-schedule and embedding-geometry ablations.
wkWQUXVuLZ.claimed_gains: DoubleCat improves TinyGSM accuracy more than threefold without an extra forward pass; SemiCat matches discrete diffusion on TinyGSM and outperforms discrete diffusion on four of six likelihood-based evaluations at 1.7B scale.
wkWQUXVuLZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the empirical ablations on CDLM design levers are thorough and that DoubleCat offers a simple, effective alternative to self-conditioning.
wkWQUXVuLZ.main_concern: Reviewers cite overlap with prior work (CANDI, Shabalin et al.) and flag a theoretical error in Section 3.1's train-inference mismatch explanation alongside weak proof that token identifiability drives the gains.

bkePv4IVoc.one_liner: Uses conformal prediction with an optimization-aware relaxation score to fix confident binary variables in repeated mixed-integer optimization.
bkePv4IVoc.problem: Learned variable fixing accelerates repeated mixed-integer optimization solves but lacks formal guarantees that fixing predicted binary variables preserves near-optimal solutions.
bkePv4IVoc.method: A learned predictor outputs binary assignments for varying problem data, and conformal prediction selects which assignments to fix using a nonconformity score measuring how far predictions must be relaxed to retain an epsilon-optimal solution. Remaining binary and continuous variables are solved by an exact MIP solver with retry-based feasibility recovery.
bkePv4IVoc.key_idea: Calibrate binary variable fixing via conformal prediction using a nonconformity score that measures the minimal relaxation needed to preserve an epsilon-optimal solution.
bkePv4IVoc.evidence: Supported by finite-sample near-optimality guarantees under i.i.d. instances and experiments on five benchmark families in control, robotics, transportation, and auctions.
bkePv4IVoc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the optimization-aware nonconformity score properly handles multiple near-optimal solutions and integrates cleanly with exact solvers and retry recovery.
bkePv4IVoc.main_concern: Experiments lack distribution-shift tests, competitive learned MIP baselines, ablations isolating conformal calibration from validation-tuned thresholds, and accounting for large offline training/calibration costs.

AvGyrJchsA.one_liner: Constructs post-hoc model ensembles by sampling parameter configurations along a nonlinear empirical loss level set without retraining.
AvGyrJchsA.problem: Post-hoc uncertainty quantification methods typically assume parametric posteriors or linear subspaces, missing nonlinear parameter-space variation among equally well-fitting models.
AvGyrJchsA.method: Level-set ENSemble (LENS) explores nonlinear directions near a fixed empirical loss level set around a trained checkpoint using Taylor-expansion geometry to collect models with similar training loss but diverse predictions. The resulting architecture-agnostic ensemble estimates predictive uncertainty without retraining.
AvGyrJchsA.key_idea: Explore nonlinear parameter-space perturbations constrained near a trained model's empirical loss level set to build a post-hoc prediction ensemble.
AvGyrJchsA.evidence: Evaluated across text, image, and tabular prediction tasks on calibration and out-of-distribution detection metrics against post-hoc uncertainty baselines.
AvGyrJchsA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the loss-level-set intuition plausible and well-motivated, though one reviewer listed no strengths and questioned advantages over deep ensembles.
AvGyrJchsA.main_concern: Reviewers criticize heavy task-specific hyperparameter tuning, lack of standard post-hoc calibration baselines like temperature scaling, and weak theoretical grounding connecting local level-set exploration to Bayesian uncertainty.

sP9w4qJKcM.one_liner: Introduces DistillBench, a unified protocol jointly evaluating unauthorized model distillation attacks, defenses, teacher utility, and acquisition costs.
sP9w4qJKcM.problem: Existing studies of unauthorized model distillation use incompatible attacker budgets, API assumptions, and utility metrics, preventing fair comparison of antidistillation defenses.
sP9w4qJKcM.method: DistillBench separates fixed or adaptive data acquisition from token-budgeted student training and jointly measures capability transfer, teacher utility, teacher similarity, detectability, and costs. The paper evaluates four distillation methods and nine defenses across four teachers and five students on math, code, and instruction following.
sP9w4qJKcM.key_idea: Standardize unauthorized distillation benchmarking by separating data acquisition from token-budgeted student training while jointly scoring transfer, teacher utility, and detectability.
sP9w4qJKcM.evidence: Evaluates four distillation methods and nine defenses across four teachers and five students on mathematical reasoning, code generation, and instruction following (with reviewers noting heavy reliance on 200 GSM8K items).
sP9w4qJKcM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly evaluating attacks, defenses, and teacher utility under standardized token budgets is a useful framework.
sP9w4qJKcM.main_concern: All three reviewers note that reported experiments omit specialized published antidistillation defenses (e.g., Antidistillation Sampling, DOGe) and rely too narrowly on 200 GSM8K questions and older Qwen2.5 students.

ioxZwqzikz.one_liner: Derives canonical representatives and operator graphs for neural computation graphs that are invariant to permutation, positive rescaling, and general linear symmetries.
ioxZwqzikz.problem: Exact parameter symmetries alter edge weights and structure in neural computation graphs without changing the computed function, making raw graph analyses unreliable.
ioxZwqzikz.method: The authors characterize minimal invariant coordinates and canonical representatives on fixed supports for positive rescaling symmetries, proving zero weights prevent a single continuous exact representation across supports. For general linear basis changes, they construct complete rank-robust operator representations, including an operator graph for multi-head attention.
ioxZwqzikz.key_idea: Canonicalizes positive-rescaling orbits on fixed supports and builds rank-complete operator graphs invariant to general linear basis changes in neural network layers.
ioxZwqzikz.evidence: Theoretical characterizations of symmetry quotients and experiments on collections of MLP and ViT checkpoints measuring stability of graph analyses and transported interventions.
ioxZwqzikz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper offers a rigorous theoretical characterization of symmetry invariance for common neural network modules and a practical preprocessing canonicalization.
ioxZwqzikz.main_concern: Reviewers note limited experimental scale without comparisons to existing equivariant weight-space models, unclear positioning relative to prior symmetry-aware networks, and dense exposition.

da2KwoffnB.one_liner: Estimates remaining constructive reasoning progress online to adaptively stop latent Chain-of-Thought inference before the fixed horizon.
da2KwoffnB.problem: Running latent Chain-of-Thought reasoners for a fixed preset horizon wastes compute and can degrade accuracy by weakening support for the correct answer in later steps.
da2KwoffnB.method: The authors decompose latent CoT dynamics into realized and remaining constructive progress, observing that later steps mainly reorganize candidates. They train a lightweight progress estimator that predicts remaining constructive progress from frozen latent states and terminates latent reasoning adaptively without retraining the LLM.
da2KwoffnB.key_idea: Predicts remaining constructive progress from intermediate latent states with a lightweight estimator to stop latent Chain-of-Thought steps adaptively on frozen models.
da2KwoffnB.evidence: Empirical analysis and evaluations across representative latent CoT reasoners (including Coconut and CODI) on multiple arithmetic benchmarks (such as GSM8K, SVAMP, and MultiArith).
da2KwoffnB.claimed_gains: Improves reasoning accuracy by up to 7.2 percentage points while reducing latent computation by up to 29.0% without retraining the LLM.
da2KwoffnB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the finding that extending latent CoT to a full fixed horizon can hurt accuracy is well demonstrated and motivates adaptive stopping.
da2KwoffnB.main_concern: Reviewers note that gains on short arithmetic benchmarks may simply reflect preset horizons exceeding gold step counts, that accuracy gains over early stopping are sometimes marginal, and that the estimator's objective mismatches signed future gain.

CHozW2lwD8.one_liner: Shapes autoencoder latent spaces into Gaussian priors via Picard-iterated Wasserstein gradient flows of a smoothed KL divergence.
CHozW2lwD8.problem: ELBO-based VAEs trade off reconstruction against prior matching, leaving the aggregate latent distribution far from Gaussian and degrading generative sample quality.
CHozW2lwD8.method: The authors define a smoothed KL divergence whose Wasserstein Gradient Flow (WGF) depends only on the smoothed score function estimated via denoising score matching. They parameterize latent trajectories with a time-conditioned neural network and iteratively align them to the WGF using semi-implicit Picard iteration alongside autoencoder training for one-step generation.
CHozW2lwD8.key_idea: Learns one-step latent trajectories aligning an autoencoder's latent distribution to a Gaussian prior by applying Picard iteration to the Wasserstein gradient flow of smoothed KL divergence.
CHozW2lwD8.evidence: Theoretical convergence proof via a Lyapunov decay argument bypassing Polyak-Lojasiewicz conditions, plus generative modeling benchmarks against VAE and few-step baselines.
CHozW2lwD8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the smoothed-KL Wasserstein gradient flow formulation and Lyapunov convergence analysis are mathematically principled and yield one-step generation.
CHozW2lwD8.main_concern: Reviewers find the empirical benchmarking insufficient and poorly matched to recent two-stage VAEs and few-step flow-map models, with unclear novelty and training scalability.

DTEznworjj.one_liner: Detects and gates irreversible agent tool calls using linear probes on internal activations and class-mean steering vectors.
DTEznworjj.problem: LLM agents rarely warn users before executing irreversible tool calls, even when explicitly prompted to flag risk.
DTEznworjj.method: The authors construct 655 tool-call argument pairs that share a function name but differ in reversibility, then train linear probes on hidden activations across 24 open-weight models to detect irreversibility. They deploy the probe as a pre-execution gate on AgentDojo and test activation steering along class-mean directions with a split-half selection check.
DTEznworjj.key_idea: Trains linear activation probes on minimal tool-call argument pairs to gate irreversible agent actions before execution and steers warnings using class-mean directions.
DTEznworjj.evidence: Probing and prompting evaluations across 24 open-weight models (1.5B-70B) and a frontier model on 655 argument pairs, plus pre-execution gating on AgentDojo.
DTEznworjj.claimed_gains: Linear probes pick the irreversible call 82.8% of the time (88.9% on six checkpoints up to 70B), whereas 91.9% of irreversible actions draw no caution under a neutral prompt; gating cuts AgentDojo prompt-injection success from 13.9% to 5.0% (8.2% with user approval of needed calls).
DTEznworjj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the representation-versus-verbalization gap for action reversibility is well motivated, consistent across many models, and carefully framed without anthropomorphizing.
DTEznworjj.main_concern: Reviewers note probe scores drift and drop in live multi-turn runs, warning detection relies on brittle regex/keyword matching, and comparisons against black-box or TF-IDF baselines are incomplete.

H7rj8l61WB.one_liner: Augments cumulative harmonic trajectory embeddings with landmark-relative angular activity summaries (ARHR) to disambiguate route orientations.
H7rj8l61WB.problem: Flattened topological harmonic embeddings capture how trajectories wind around landmarks but fail to distinguish routes with equal cumulative winding and different landmark-relative orientations.
H7rj8l61WB.method: Azimuth-Resolved Harmonic Representation (ARHR) concatenates a compact summary of landmark-relative angular activity onto the cumulative harmonic trajectory embedding without training. The paper also derives azimuth-shift equivariance and sufficient conditions for separating trajectories with identical cumulative harmonic responses.
H7rj8l61WB.key_idea: Supplements cumulative harmonic trajectory embeddings with a training-free summary of landmark-relative angular Fourier activity to resolve orientation ambiguity.
H7rj8l61WB.evidence: Analytical conditions for route discrimination, clustering experiments on real-world and synthetic traffic datasets, and weighting and angular-order ablations.
H7rj8l61WB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the orientation ambiguity of harmonic trajectory embeddings is clearly motivated and ARHR provides a simple, training-free addition with clean analytical properties.
H7rj8l61WB.main_concern: Reviewers view the contribution as incremental and point out that ARHR does not consistently beat simpler geometric baselines like Frechet distance or endpoint-augmented harmonics.

UoioJWwjam.one_liner: Benchmarks personal assistant memory for evolving interaction preferences across 99 on-policy sessions per simulated user.
UoioJWwjam.problem: Existing agent memory benchmarks focus on factual recall rather than learning when to clarify, confirm, or act autonomously according to context-dependent, evolving user interaction preferences.
UoioJWwjam.method: The authors introduce MemPA, an on-policy interactive environment featuring four grounded simulated users with 14 preferences across work and personal contexts over 99 sessions and four months, including five event-driven preference changes per user. They decompose evaluation into preference acquisition, selection (PSA, CS, PET), and behavioral realization against No Memory and Oracle baselines.
UoioJWwjam.key_idea: Evaluates assistant memory on-policy across 99 longitudinal sessions with event-driven preference updates, separating preference acquisition, context-sensitive selection, and behavioral realization.
UoioJWwjam.evidence: Evaluations of four memory systems (Mem0, MemOS, simple RAG, and File-based memory) across four LLM backbones on the four-user, 99-session benchmark.
UoioJWwjam.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the on-policy formulation and diagnostic decomposition into acquisition, selection, context sensitivity, and preference evolution are well motivated and informative.
UoioJWwjam.main_concern: Reviewers highlight limited breadth with only four users, heavy author adjudication of ground-truth preference cells for two users, unrealistic always-explicit user feedback, and missing comparisons to recent personalized-agent benchmarks.

P3KiLNMpLR.one_liner: Pairs candidate-conditioned auditing with a sealed task-only diagnostic proposer and budgeted knapsack selection to overcome missing support.
P3KiLNMpLR.problem: Collaborative LLM auditing suffers from candidate anchoring, where candidate-conditioned proposers omit diagnostic checks needed to expose latent errors so downstream selection cannot recover them.
P3KiLNMpLR.method: The paper separates diagnostic action generation from budgeted allocation in a two-stage auditing framework. A sealed task-only proposer commits diagnostic checks before seeing the candidate solution, pooling them with candidate-conditioned checks for route-blind budgeted selection based on calibrated proxy value from shared triage and reconstruction evidence.
P3KiLNMpLR.key_idea: Generates diagnostic checks from a sealed task-only proposer before seeing the candidate and pools them with candidate-conditioned checks for budgeted selection.
P3KiLNMpLR.evidence: Controlled linear programming auditing case study with 300 injected errors across four error families and 150 paired correct controls, plus nomination-selection-repair decomposition.
P3KiLNMpLR.claimed_gains: Task-only supplementation recovers 66 of the 122 error targets omitted by the candidate-conditioned route, and every recovered target is purchased and repaired.
P3KiLNMpLR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating check coverage, selection, and repair clearly diagnoses auditing failures, and note the controlled LP benchmark honestly tracks errors and harm.
P3KiLNMpLR.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the task-only proposer's four keyword-sorted strata map one-to-one onto the four planted error families, and that stratified random nomination outperforms the proposed scoring order.

g2fvIF5XDW.one_liner: Benchmarks multi-agent error recovery under misaligned, incomplete, and missed colleague responses using program-verified scenarios.
g2fvIF5XDW.problem: Multi-agent evaluations typically assume perfect collaborators who always provide accurate, complete, and timely information, hiding failure modes when teammates are unreliable.
g2fvIF5XDW.method: The authors introduce UnCoBench (also named CollabStress in the TL;DR), pairing reliable tasks with Misaligned, Incomplete, and Missed colleague failure settings so a main agent must verify context, diagnose gaps, and follow up. Scenarios are generated via an LLM pipeline paired with executable checks enforcing answer uniqueness and role necessity.
g2fvIF5XDW.key_idea: Tests multi-agent robustness using paired reliable and unreliable colleague policies (Misaligned, Incomplete, Missed) validated by executable uniqueness and role-necessity checks.
g2fvIF5XDW.evidence: Evaluations across ten LLM models on paired reliable and unreliable scenarios, plus trace analysis and a human audit of validation decisions.
g2fvIF5XDW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree unreliable multi-agent collaboration is an important underexplored problem and praise the paired controlled design with executable benchmark validation checks.
g2fvIF5XDW.main_concern: Reviewers question how realistic the scripted colleague failure policies are, how the setup differs from single-agent noisy tool use or hidden-information benchmarks, and note missing code and dataset release.

w5JIq6g3cZ.one_liner: Generalizes supervised contrastive loss into a cross-entropy over inverted pairwise distances between crowdsourced soft-label histograms.
w5JIq6g3cZ.problem: Standard contrastive learning assumes single hard class labels and discards annotator disagreement signals present in crowdsourced multi-annotator datasets.
w5JIq6g3cZ.method: The authors rewrite supervised and unsupervised contrastive losses as cross-entropy and replace the target distribution with inverted distances between normalized annotation-histogram soft labels (SDSL). They also derive a theoretical link between the contrastive risk and downstream soft-label linear classification risk.
w5JIq6g3cZ.key_idea: Replaces binary positive/negative targets in contrastive cross-entropy with a continuous target distribution defined by inverted distances between crowdsourced soft-label histograms.
w5JIq6g3cZ.evidence: Theoretical risk analysis connecting contrastive and linear-probe risks, plus experiments on real-world image classification and sleep staging datasets.
w5JIq6g3cZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the soft-label contrastive formulation is simple, interpretable, well written, and backed by a useful theoretical link to downstream linear classification.
w5JIq6g3cZ.main_concern: Reviewers flag limited novelty and imprecise positioning relative to prior soft-label contrastive learning and crowdsourcing methods like CrowdCons, plus confounded comparisons against SupCon.

WpT2WXSF4v.one_liner: Fuses RGB and event features in a dual-branch Mamba network using a closed-form Fourier damped-wave propagator and cross-modal coupling.
WpT2WXSF4v.problem: Low-light semantic segmentation degrades on RGB frames while existing RGB-event fusion modules ignore that events carry high-frequency dynamics and frames carry low-frequency structure.
WpT2WXSF4v.method: MambaFourier embeds a Wave-Fourier Fusion (WFF) block at each scale of a dual-branch state-space network, applying a real FFT, a learnable per-channel damped-wave propagator, a band-limited filter, a reciprocal 2x2 cross-modal coupling matrix, and an inverse FFT. Parameters are mode-indexed for resolution transfer and initialized as an exact identity.
WpT2WXSF4v.key_idea: Performs RGB-event fusion in the Fourier domain via a closed-form damped-wave propagator, a band-limited filter, and reciprocal 2x2 cross-modal mode coupling.
WpT2WXSF4v.evidence: Semantic segmentation benchmarks on DDD17, DSEC-Semantic, DERS-XS, and DSEC-Xtrm, synthetic rain and fog tests, and component ablations.
WpT2WXSF4v.claimed_gains: Reaches 79.39% mIoU on DDD17 (+1.83% over MambaSeg), 75.65% on DSEC-Semantic (+4.61% over ESC), 70.40% on DERS-XS (+3.30% over ESC), and 56.51% on DSEC-Xtrm (+5.64% over the previous best).
WpT2WXSF4v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the spectral RGB-event fusion design is clearly formulated and achieves solid empirical segmentation results with helpful ablations.
WpT2WXSF4v.main_concern: Reviewers question the physical wave-field interpretation and high-frequency claims because cross-modal coupling is learned only on a small low-frequency subset (5.7% of rFFT2 coefficients at stage 1).

DBFIcHXVE3.one_liner: Certifies machine unlearning for students distilled from a black-box teacher by re-distilling on retained data and adding calibrated Gaussian noise.
DBFIcHXVE3.problem: After deploying a distilled student, deleting forget samples is hard to certify when the teacher is inaccessible for retraining and only exposes black-box prediction queries.
DBFIcHXVE3.method: The framework (CKDU) re-distills the student on the retained dataset using black-box queries to the original teacher and perturbs the resulting parameters with calibrated Gaussian noise. The noise scale is derived by bounding how teacher predictions would shift if retrained without the forget set and propagating that sensitivity through the distillation objective.
DBFIcHXVE3.key_idea: Bounds teacher prediction shift under counterfactual retraining, propagates it to student distillation sensitivity, and perturbs re-distilled student weights with calibrated Gaussian noise.
DBFIcHXVE3.evidence: Theoretical sensitivity and certification proofs for convex and non-convex student losses, plus experiments on simplified models such as one-hidden-layer tanh networks.
DBFIcHXVE3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly shows naive re-distillation on the original teacher fails unlearning and provides a modular, mathematically sound theoretical proof chain.
DBFIcHXVE3.main_concern: Reviewers note the certificate requires detailed white-box knowledge of teacher training hyperparameters and shared inputs, becomes vacuous unless the teacher is nearly frozen, and exhibits numerical inconsistencies in tables.

gD9vE0p1e0.one_liner: Separates append-only affective evidence logging at write time from access-time longitudinal claim reconstruction as a host-modular memory layer.
gD9vE0p1e0.problem: Memory-augmented LLM agents often lose cross-time relationships across affective histories when they compress or retrieve isolated interactions.
gD9vE0p1e0.method: AffectLedger stores source-grounded local affective observations in an append-only ledger at write time without altering the host memory system. At access time, it retrieves a bounded historical evidence sequence and reconstructs compact, evidence-linked claims making cross-time relationships explicit to supplement the host's context.
gD9vE0p1e0.key_idea: Logs raw local affective observations in an append-only ledger at write time and reconstructs bounded, evidence-linked cross-time claims only at memory access time.
gD9vE0p1e0.evidence: Evaluations across five heterogeneous memory hosts and two CloneMem history scales, plus controlled factorial ablations and paired statistical tests.
gD9vE0p1e0.claimed_gains: Improves accuracy in all ten comparisons across five hosts and two CloneMem history scales by +3.10 to +13.98 percentage points.
gD9vE0p1e0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the modular host-agnostic design is clearly written and produces consistent accuracy improvements across all five evaluated memory hosts.
gD9vE0p1e0.main_concern: Reviewers find the technical increment over prior temporal/episodic memory layers and generic summarization unclear, noting that exposing selected raw evidence or generic reconstruction matches or beats relation-aware reconstruction.

FdtAdPaxYj.one_liner: Uses multi-agent LLM coordination and Monte Carlo tree search to jointly evolve MILP parameters, dynamic policies, and cut/branching rules.
FdtAdPaxYj.problem: Automated MILP algorithm design typically tunes parameters or evolves heuristics for one solver component at a time, missing gains from coordinated cross-component changes.
FdtAdPaxYj.method: CoMILP jointly optimizes initial parameters, dynamic configuration policies, and cut-selection and branching rules using coordinated LLM agents that select components and edit types, propose local updates, and reflect on solver feedback. Tree search retains alternative refinement paths to balance exploration and exploitation.
FdtAdPaxYj.key_idea: Coordinates LLM agents with tree search and solver feedback to jointly evolve initial MILP parameters, dynamic policies, and cut-selection and branching decision rules.
FdtAdPaxYj.evidence: Evaluations on MIPLIB 2017 and five additional MILP problem families against solver-design baselines, along with component ablations.
FdtAdPaxYj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree jointly optimizing interacting MILP solver components is a well-motivated problem and praise the broad evaluation across MIPLIB 2017 and generated benchmarks.
FdtAdPaxYj.main_concern: Reviewers note that main results rely on 100 instance-specific adaptation trials with weak generalization evidence, and that no non-LLM search baseline isolates the value of LLM reasoning over the enlarged search space.

eDHudhsWqj.one_liner: Combines AdaBelief-style variance normalization with LaProp-style post-normalization momentum in an Adam-like stochastic optimizer.
eDHudhsWqj.problem: Standard Adam-type optimizers couple stale momentum with stochastic normalizers and collapse toward sign updates in low-variance regimes.
eDHudhsWqj.method: MVN-Grad scales each coordinate by an exponential moving average of gradient variance and applies momentum to the variance-normalized gradients rather than before normalization, supported by one-step variance, spike-response, limiting-dynamics, and nonconvex convergence analyses.
eDHudhsWqj.key_idea: Normalize stochastic gradients by an exponential moving average of gradient variance before accumulating them into the momentum buffer.
eDHudhsWqj.evidence: Theoretical variance and nonconvex convergence proofs plus experiments on CIFAR-100 (ResNet18) and GPT-style language models up to 350M parameters against Adam, AdaBelief, and LaProp.
eDHudhsWqj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the motivation for decoupling normalization and momentum is clearly presented and backed by detailed theoretical derivations and consistent empirical results.
eDHudhsWqj.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty over AdaBelief, LaProp, and centered RMSProp, note limited experimental breadth, and argue that one-step variance bounds do not establish trajectory-level stability or better generalization.

h3sMHdywNM.one_liner: Applies Gauss-Newton and Hessian continuation to adapt only small linear output heads on frozen multi-head PINN bases for nonlinear PDEs.
h3sMHdywNM.problem: One-shot transfer learning on frozen PINN bases lacks direct closed-form head solves for nonlinear PDEs, forcing prior work to approximate nonlinear terms.
h3sMHdywNM.method: The authors train multi-head PINNs to learn a low-dimensional shared basis across PDE parameters and initial conditions, then freeze the basis and solve for unseen nonlinear PDE head weights directly using Gauss-Newton optimization and Hessian continuation to trace weight-space solution paths.
h3sMHdywNM.key_idea: Freeze a learned low-dimensional multi-head PINN basis so unseen nonlinear PDE instances can be solved directly in head-weight space via Gauss-Newton and Hessian continuation.
h3sMHdywNM.evidence: Evaluated on families of linear and nonlinear PDEs with varying equation parameters and initial conditions, comparing speed and accuracy primarily against Adam.
h3sMHdywNM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that restricting second-order optimization to a small frozen linear head makes nonlinear PINN adaptation fast and well-presented.
h3sMHdywNM.main_concern: Reviewers note missing comparisons against strong head solvers, nonlinear OTL baselines, and meta-learning PINN methods, and question the practical utility of slower Hessian continuation over Gauss-Newton.

YvrtNbSjDZ.one_liner: Replaces KV-cache projections with a codebook-free finite scalar quantization bottleneck and decodes directly via a fused Triton kernel.
YvrtNbSjDZ.problem: KV-cache memory grows linearly with context length and exceeds consumer device budgets, while existing compression methods fail at extreme compression ratios.
YvrtNbSjDZ.method: Transformer-FSQ replaces standard key and value projections with a finite scalar quantization bottleneck storing packed integer codes per token without codebooks or per-token scale metadata, trained on 0.25 tokens per parameter with frozen weights and decoded via a fused Triton kernel.
YvrtNbSjDZ.key_idea: Project tokens into shared low-bit discrete integer latents via codebook-free finite scalar quantization and compute attention directly from packed codes in a fused Triton kernel.
YvrtNbSjDZ.evidence: Evaluated against five baseline families on 0.6B to 8B models (including Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B/8B) on RULER long-context retrieval and decode throughput benchmarks.
YvrtNbSjDZ.claimed_gains: Achieves the highest RULER accuracy from 12x to 97.5x compression across scales, and decodes Qwen3-8B-Base at 1.01x (95% CI 0.98-1.05) native SDPA throughput at 32x and 1.54x at 97.5x.
YvrtNbSjDZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean, metadata-free discrete latent design combining dimension reduction with low-bit quantization and its strong accuracy-compression trade-off at high compression ratios.
YvrtNbSjDZ.main_concern: Reviewers highlight that bfloat16 activation noise collapses accuracy, forcing float32 execution that doubles weight memory, and that favorable accuracy and speed regimes barely overlap.

JufUpEAiLN.one_liner: Probes V-JEPA 2 predictors for object permanence by comparing hidden-region predictions against encoder representations of present versus absent worlds.
JufUpEAiLN.problem: Standard prediction-error tests of object permanence in video world models are confounded because empty regions are easier to predict than moving objects.
JufUpEAiLN.method: The authors compare frozen V-JEPA 2 predictor outputs in occluded regions against encoder representations of two worlds differing only in the hidden object, validating the readout on predictors trained with known object-persistence probabilities across stationary, moving, and boxed-object scenes.
JufUpEAiLN.key_idea: Read out hidden-object belief by comparing the predictor's latent output against encoder embeddings of counterfactual present-versus-absent scenes rather than raw prediction error.
JufUpEAiLN.evidence: Evaluated across three V-JEPA 2 encoder scales on rendered occlusion scenes and real occlusion videos, plus controlled curricula.
JufUpEAiLN.claimed_gains: In rendered scenes across three encoder scales, a stationary hidden ball is read as present in 70-91% of scenes over 3.5 s, whereas a moving ball persists for only 0.5-1.1 s and a ball inside a moving box is not kept.
JufUpEAiLN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that testing object permanence in video world models is an important question and appreciate the varied occlusion controls.
JufUpEAiLN.main_concern: Reviewers criticize poor, dense writing that is hard to follow, limited real-world evaluation sharing the same renderer for training and probing, and an unclear link between the readout score and actual retained memory.
